//! Fixed-capacity cooperative kernel-thread smoke runtime.
//!
//! Thread stacks are allocator-owned 4 KiB mappings with one unmapped lower
//! guard page. Scheduling is single-vCPU and cooperative only; the timer IRQ
//! never switches contexts or mutates scheduler state.

use crate::kprintln;
use core::arch::asm;
use core::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering};
use rustix_kernel::frame::{Frame, FrameAllocator};

use rustix_kernel::paging::{
    validate_mapping_range, CachePolicy, CandidatePageTableMemory, CandidatePageTables,
    EffectiveMemoryType, MtrrState, PagePermissions, PageWalkOutcome, PatLayout, PAGE_SIZE,
};
use rustix_kernel::scheduler::{
    initialize_thread_context_stack, Scheduler, SchedulerError, ThreadId, ThreadState, WaitQueueId,
};
use rustix_kernel::time::AtomicTickCounter;

const MAX_THREADS: usize = 2;
const THREAD_STACK_PAGES: usize = 4;
const THREAD_STACK_STRIDE: u64 = (THREAD_STACK_PAGES as u64 + 1) * PAGE_SIZE;
const THREAD_STACK_VIRTUAL_BASE: u64 = 0xffff_c400_0000_0000;
const CONTEXT_COUNT: usize = MAX_THREADS + 1;
const QUEUE_COUNT: usize = MAX_THREADS + 1;
const _: [(); QUEUE_COUNT] = [(); MAX_THREADS + 1];

static THREAD_TEST_TRACE: AtomicUsize = AtomicUsize::new(0);

type ThreadEntry = extern "C" fn(*mut (), usize);

struct KernelThreadRuntime {
    policy: Scheduler<MAX_THREADS, QUEUE_COUNT, MAX_THREADS>,
    saved_rsp: [usize; CONTEXT_COUNT],
    thread_ids: [Option<ThreadId>; MAX_THREADS],
    stack_virtual_starts: [Option<u64>; MAX_THREADS],
    entries: [Option<ThreadEntry>; MAX_THREADS],
    arguments: [usize; MAX_THREADS],
    deadlines: [Option<u64>; MAX_THREADS],
    event_queue: WaitQueueId,
    timer_queues: [WaitQueueId; MAX_THREADS],
    current_context: usize,
    input_events_enabled: bool,
    ticks: &'static AtomicTickCounter,
}

impl KernelThreadRuntime {
    fn new(ticks: &'static AtomicTickCounter) -> Result<Self, SchedulerError> {
        let mut policy = Scheduler::new();
        let event_queue = policy.create_wait_queue()?;
        let mut timer_queues = [event_queue; MAX_THREADS];
        for queue in &mut timer_queues {
            *queue = policy.create_wait_queue()?;
        }
        Ok(Self {
            policy,
            saved_rsp: [0; CONTEXT_COUNT],
            thread_ids: [None; MAX_THREADS],
            stack_virtual_starts: [None; MAX_THREADS],
            entries: [None; MAX_THREADS],
            arguments: [0; MAX_THREADS],
            deadlines: [None; MAX_THREADS],
            event_queue,
            timer_queues,
            current_context: 0,
            input_events_enabled: false,
            ticks,
        })
    }

    fn all_threads_exited(&self) -> bool {
        self.thread_ids
            .iter()
            .flatten()
            .all(|thread| self.policy.state(*thread) == Ok(ThreadState::Exited))
    }

    fn wake_expired(&mut self) {
        let now = self.ticks.ticks();
        for slot in 0..MAX_THREADS {
            if self.deadlines[slot].is_some_and(|deadline| now >= deadline) {
                self.deadlines[slot] = None;
                if self.policy.wake_one(self.timer_queues[slot]).is_err() {
                    THREAD_TEST_TRACE.store(99, Ordering::Release);
                }
            }
        }
    }

    fn poll_wakeups(&mut self) -> bool {
        self.wake_expired();
        let input_event = self.input_events_enabled
            && rustix_kernel::input::INPUT_EVENT_PENDING.swap(false, Ordering::AcqRel);
        if input_event && self.policy.wake_all(self.event_queue).is_err() {
            THREAD_TEST_TRACE.store(99, Ordering::Release);
        }
        input_event
    }

    unsafe fn run_from_raw(runtime_pointer: *mut Self) {
        let initial_flags = disable_interrupts();
        let first = {
            // SAFETY: The caller supplies the live, exclusively owned runtime;
            // the temporary reference ends before the context switch.
            let runtime = unsafe { &mut *runtime_pointer };
            match runtime.policy.dispatch() {
                Ok(Some(thread)) => {
                    let context = thread.slot_index() + 1;
                    runtime.current_context = context;
                    Some(runtime.saved_rsp[context])
                }
                Ok(None) => None,
                Err(_) => {
                    THREAD_TEST_TRACE.store(99, Ordering::Release);
                    None
                }
            }
        };
        if let Some(new_rsp) = first {
            // SAFETY: Context zero is the active bootstrap stack; `new_rsp` is a
            // synthetic, ABI-aligned frame on a mapped owned thread stack.
            unsafe {
                rustix_arch_context_switch(
                    core::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*runtime_pointer).saved_rsp[0]),
                    new_rsp as *mut usize,
                );
            }
        }
        restore_interrupts(initial_flags);

        loop {
            let flags = disable_interrupts();
            let (new_rsp, finished) = {
                // SAFETY: No other thread runs while IF is clear. All mutable
                // scheduler borrows end before any subsequent context switch.
                let runtime = unsafe { &mut *runtime_pointer };
                runtime.poll_wakeups();
                if runtime.all_threads_exited() {
                    (None, true)
                } else {
                    match runtime.policy.dispatch() {
                        Ok(Some(thread)) => {
                            let context = thread.slot_index() + 1;
                            runtime.current_context = context;
                            (Some(runtime.saved_rsp[context]), false)
                        }
                        Ok(None) => (None, false),
                        Err(_) => {
                            THREAD_TEST_TRACE.store(99, Ordering::Release);
                            (None, true)
                        }
                    }
                }
            };
            if finished {
                restore_interrupts(flags);
                return;
            }
            if let Some(new_rsp) = new_rsp {
                // SAFETY: The bootstrap context is currently active and the
                // selected thread owns a live saved stack frame.
                unsafe {
                    rustix_arch_context_switch(
                        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*runtime_pointer).saved_rsp[0]),
                        new_rsp as *mut usize,
                    );
                }
                restore_interrupts(flags);
            } else {
                // `sti; hlt` is atomic with respect to the interrupt shadow, so
                // a PIT wakeup cannot be lost between checking deadlines and halt.
                // SAFETY: The verified PIT handler is installed and the only
                // unmasked device route; it performs no allocation or scheduling.
                unsafe { asm!("sti; hlt") };
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Run a single long-lived cooperative worker on an owned guarded stack.
pub fn run_shell<M: CandidatePageTableMemory>(
    candidate: &mut CandidatePageTables<'_, M>,
    allocator: *mut FrameAllocator,
    cpu_info: &crate::arch::x86_64::cpu::CpuInfo,
    ticks: &'static AtomicTickCounter,
    entry: extern "C" fn(*mut (), usize),
    argument: usize,
) -> ! {
    let mut runtime =
        KernelThreadRuntime::new(ticks).unwrap_or_else(|_| halt_on_stack_cleanup_failure());
    runtime.input_events_enabled = true;
    let runtime_pointer = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(runtime);
    let flags = disable_interrupts();
    // SAFETY: The caller supplies the live allocator retained by BootInfo. This
    // exclusive borrow is limited to stack setup and ends before context switches.
    let spawned = unsafe {
        spawn_thread(
            &mut runtime,
            candidate,
            &mut *allocator,
            cpu_info,
            runtime_pointer,
            entry,
            argument,
        )
    };
    if spawned.is_err() {
        restore_interrupts(flags);
        halt_on_stack_cleanup_failure();
    }
    restore_interrupts(flags);
    // SAFETY: The caller keeps the active root, allocator, CPU snapshot, thread
    // context, and callback argument alive for this non-returning kernel runtime.
    unsafe { KernelThreadRuntime::run_from_raw(runtime_pointer) };
    let flags = disable_interrupts();
    // SAFETY: No worker is running after `run_from_raw` returns, so the raw
    // allocator pointer is exclusively available for final stack cleanup.
    let allocator = unsafe { &mut *allocator };
    reap_exited_stacks(&mut runtime, candidate, allocator);
    restore_interrupts(flags);
    halt_on_stack_cleanup_failure()
}

/// Block the current cooperative thread until an input IRQ publishes an event.
pub(crate) fn wait_for_input(runtime_pointer: *mut ()) {
    // SAFETY: Only a normal cooperative thread calls this; IRQ handlers merely
    // publish the atomic event and never touch scheduler policy state.
    if !unsafe { block_current(runtime_pointer.cast(), None) } {
        THREAD_TEST_TRACE.store(99, Ordering::Release);
    }
}

/// Exercise real cooperative switching, stack guards, event wakeup, and timed sleep.
/// The caller must provide the current active root, keep this single-vCPU kernel
/// path alive for the call, and have already enabled the verified PIT route. The
/// timer handler only increments `ticks` and acknowledges the local APIC; all
/// scheduler transitions happen on ordinary kernel stacks with IF controlled here.
#[cfg(feature = "probe-kernel-threads")]
pub fn smoke<M: CandidatePageTableMemory>(
    candidate: &mut CandidatePageTables<'_, M>,
    allocator: &mut FrameAllocator,
    cpu_info: &crate::arch::x86_64::cpu::CpuInfo,
    ticks: &'static AtomicTickCounter,
) -> Result<(), &'static str> {
    THREAD_TEST_TRACE.store(0, Ordering::Release);
    let mut runtime = KernelThreadRuntime::new(ticks).map_err(|_| "scheduler setup failed")?;
    let runtime_pointer = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(runtime);

    let flags = disable_interrupts();
    let first = spawn_thread(
        &mut runtime,
        candidate,
        allocator,
        cpu_info,
        runtime_pointer,
        waiter_thread,
        0,
    );
    let second = if first.is_ok() {
        spawn_thread(
            &mut runtime,
            candidate,
            allocator,
            cpu_info,
            runtime_pointer,
            signaler_thread,
            0,
        )
    } else {
        Err("waiter thread stack setup failed")
    };
    restore_interrupts(flags);

    if first.is_err() || second.is_err() {
        cancel_unstarted_threads(&mut runtime);
        let flags = disable_interrupts();
        reap_exited_stacks(&mut runtime, candidate, allocator);
        restore_interrupts(flags);
        return Err(first
            .err()
            .or(second.err())
            .unwrap_or("thread setup failed"));
    }

    // Every stack slot was checked page by page during setup: the lower guard is
    // absent, and all four stack leaves are supervisor RW/NX with the selected WB type.
    kprintln!("kernel thread stacks verified: mapped RW/NX with absent lower guards");
    // SAFETY: The runtime remains on the bootstrap stack and is passed by raw
    // pointer; no mutable reference is retained across the context switches.
    unsafe { KernelThreadRuntime::run_from_raw(runtime_pointer) };

    let passed = THREAD_TEST_TRACE.load(Ordering::Acquire) == 5
        && ticks.ticks() >= 2
        && runtime.all_threads_exited();
    let flags = disable_interrupts();
    reap_exited_stacks(&mut runtime, candidate, allocator);
    restore_interrupts(flags);
    if !passed {
        return Err("cooperative yield/wakeup/timed-sleep sequence failed");
    }
    kprintln!("cooperative thread path passed: yield, event wakeup, timed sleep, stack guards");
    Ok(())
}

fn spawn_thread<M: CandidatePageTableMemory>(
    runtime: &mut KernelThreadRuntime,
    candidate: &mut CandidatePageTables<'_, M>,
    allocator: &mut FrameAllocator,
    cpu_info: &crate::arch::x86_64::cpu::CpuInfo,
    runtime_pointer: *mut KernelThreadRuntime,
    entry: ThreadEntry,
    argument: usize,
) -> Result<ThreadId, &'static str> {
    let slot = runtime
        .thread_ids
        .iter()
        .position(Option::is_none)
        .ok_or("thread capacity exhausted")?;
    let region_start = THREAD_STACK_VIRTUAL_BASE
        .checked_add(
            (slot as u64)
                .checked_mul(THREAD_STACK_STRIDE)
                .ok_or("stack VA overflow")?,
        )
        .ok_or("stack VA overflow")?;
    let stack_start = region_start
        .checked_add(PAGE_SIZE)
        .ok_or("stack VA overflow")?;

    for page in 0..=THREAD_STACK_PAGES {
        let address = region_start + page as u64 * PAGE_SIZE;
        if !matches!(
            candidate.walk(address),
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::NotPresent { .. })
        ) {
            return Err("thread guard or stack VA is already mapped");
        }
    }

    let physical_width = cpu_info
        .physical_address_bits
        .ok_or("physical width unavailable")?;
    let pat = PatLayout::from_msr_value(cpu_info.pat_msr_value.ok_or("PAT unavailable")?)
        .map_err(|_| "PAT state invalid")?;
    let mtrrs = match &cpu_info.mtrr {
        MtrrState::Captured(registers) => registers
            .validated_layout(physical_width)
            .map_err(|_| "MTRR state invalid")?,
        _ => return Err("MTRR state unavailable"),
    };
    let permissions = PagePermissions {
        writable: true,
        executable: false,
        user_accessible: false,
    };
    let mut mapped_pages = 0usize;
    for page in 0..THREAD_STACK_PAGES {
        let virtual_address = stack_start + page as u64 * PAGE_SIZE;
        let frame = allocator.allocate().ok_or_else(|| {
            rollback_stack(candidate, allocator, stack_start, mapped_pages);
            "physical frames exhausted for thread stack"
        })?;
        let mapping = match validate_mapping_range(
            virtual_address,
            frame.address(),
            PAGE_SIZE,
            permissions,
            Some(physical_width),
            cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        ) {
            Ok(mapping) => mapping,
            Err(_) => {
                deallocate_or_halt(allocator, frame);
                rollback_stack(candidate, allocator, stack_start, mapped_pages);
                return Err("thread stack mapping rejected");
            }
        };
        let attributes = match mapping.select_cache_attributes(
            CachePolicy::WriteBack,
            pat,
            &mtrrs,
            cpu_info.normal_caching,
        ) {
            Ok(attributes) if attributes.effective_type() == EffectiveMemoryType::WriteBack => {
                attributes
            }
            _ => {
                deallocate_or_halt(allocator, frame);
                rollback_stack(candidate, allocator, stack_start, mapped_pages);
                return Err("thread stack has no uniform write-back policy");
            }
        };
        // SAFETY: The active root is current on this single CPU; IF is clear
        // throughout stack setup, and each mapping uses an allocator-owned frame.
        if let Err(failure) =
            unsafe { candidate.map_owned_page_active(allocator, frame, mapping, attributes) }
        {
            deallocate_or_halt(allocator, failure.frame);
            rollback_stack(candidate, allocator, stack_start, mapped_pages);
            return Err("thread stack mapping failed");
        }
        match candidate.walk(virtual_address) {
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation))
                if translation.permissions == permissions
                    && translation.pat_index == attributes.pat_index() => {}
            _ => {
                rollback_stack(candidate, allocator, stack_start, mapped_pages + 1);
                return Err("thread stack page-table verification failed");
            }
        }
        mapped_pages += 1;
    }

    let stack_top = stack_start + THREAD_STACK_PAGES as u64 * PAGE_SIZE;
    let frame_word_count = 16;
    let frame_words = unsafe {
        core::slice::from_raw_parts_mut(
            (stack_top as *mut usize).sub(frame_word_count),
            frame_word_count,
        )
    };
    let registers = [0, slot, runtime_pointer as usize, 0, 0, 0];
    let saved_rsp = initialize_thread_context_stack(
        frame_words,
        registers,
        kernel_thread_trampoline as *const () as usize,
    );
    let Some(saved_rsp) = saved_rsp else {
        rollback_stack(candidate, allocator, stack_start, mapped_pages);
        return Err("thread initial context frame did not fit");
    };
    let thread = match runtime.policy.create_thread() {
        Ok(thread) if thread.slot_index() == slot => thread,
        Ok(_) => {
            rollback_stack(candidate, allocator, stack_start, mapped_pages);
            return Err("scheduler slot and stack slot diverged");
        }
        Err(_) => {
            rollback_stack(candidate, allocator, stack_start, mapped_pages);
            return Err("scheduler thread capacity exhausted");
        }
    };
    runtime.thread_ids[slot] = Some(thread);
    runtime.stack_virtual_starts[slot] = Some(stack_start);
    runtime.entries[slot] = Some(entry);
    runtime.arguments[slot] = argument;
    runtime.saved_rsp[slot + 1] = saved_rsp;
    Ok(thread)
}

fn rollback_stack<M: CandidatePageTableMemory>(
    candidate: &mut CandidatePageTables<'_, M>,
    allocator: &mut FrameAllocator,
    stack_start: u64,
    mapped_pages: usize,
) {
    for page in (0..mapped_pages).rev() {
        let virtual_address = stack_start + page as u64 * PAGE_SIZE;
        // SAFETY: Stack setup keeps IF clear and this candidate is the active
        // root; the frame is not returned until `invlpg` completes.
        let frame = unsafe { candidate.unmap_owned_page_active(virtual_address) }
            .unwrap_or_else(|_| halt_on_stack_cleanup_failure());
        deallocate_or_halt(allocator, frame);
    }
}

fn reap_exited_stacks<M: CandidatePageTableMemory>(
    runtime: &mut KernelThreadRuntime,
    candidate: &mut CandidatePageTables<'_, M>,
    allocator: &mut FrameAllocator,
) {
    for slot in 0..MAX_THREADS {
        let Some(thread) = runtime.thread_ids[slot] else {
            continue;
        };
        if runtime.policy.state(thread) != Ok(ThreadState::Exited) {
            continue;
        }
        let stack_start =
            runtime.stack_virtual_starts[slot].unwrap_or_else(|| halt_on_stack_cleanup_failure());
        rollback_stack(candidate, allocator, stack_start, THREAD_STACK_PAGES);
        runtime
            .policy
            .reap(thread)
            .unwrap_or_else(|_| halt_on_stack_cleanup_failure());
        runtime.thread_ids[slot] = None;
        runtime.stack_virtual_starts[slot] = None;
        runtime.entries[slot] = None;
        runtime.arguments[slot] = 0;
        runtime.deadlines[slot] = None;
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-kernel-threads")]
fn cancel_unstarted_threads(runtime: &mut KernelThreadRuntime) {
    loop {
        match runtime.policy.dispatch() {
            Ok(Some(_)) => {
                if runtime.policy.exit_current().is_err() {
                    halt_on_stack_cleanup_failure();
                }
            }
            Ok(None) => return,
            Err(_) => halt_on_stack_cleanup_failure(),
        }
    }
}

fn deallocate_or_halt(allocator: &mut FrameAllocator, frame: Frame) {
    if let Err(failure) = allocator.deallocate(frame) {
        kprintln!("thread stack frame release failed: {:?}", failure.error);
        halt_on_stack_cleanup_failure();
    }
}

fn halt_on_stack_cleanup_failure() -> ! {
    loop {
        // SAFETY: Losing stack-frame ownership is fatal; stop without touching
        // any potentially inconsistent scheduler or allocator state.
        unsafe { asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    }
}

extern "C" fn kernel_thread_trampoline() -> ! {
    let runtime_pointer: *mut KernelThreadRuntime;
    let slot: usize;
    // SAFETY: The initial stack frame restores the runtime pointer in R13 and
    // the generation-checked policy slot index in R14 before this entry.
    unsafe {
        asm!("mov {}, r13", out(reg) runtime_pointer, options(nomem, nostack, preserves_flags));
        asm!("mov {}, r14", out(reg) slot, options(nomem, nostack, preserves_flags));
    }
    let (entry, argument) = {
        // SAFETY: The runtime is live on the retained bootstrap stack and the
        // selected slot was initialized before its context became dispatchable.
        let runtime = unsafe { &*runtime_pointer };
        let entry = runtime.entries[slot].unwrap_or_else(|| halt_on_stack_cleanup_failure());
        (entry, runtime.arguments[slot])
    };
    // New cooperative contexts start with IF clear. Enable the already-verified
    // timer route only after their descriptor and runtime state are available.
    // SAFETY: The scheduler installs no thread until the caller has configured
    // the timer and registered its bounded non-scheduling handler.
    unsafe { asm!("sti") };
    entry(runtime_pointer.cast(), argument);
    // SAFETY: This thread's entry returned normally; mark it exited and switch
    // away before its stack can be reclaimed by the bootstrap context.
    unsafe { exit_current(runtime_pointer) }
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-kernel-threads")]
extern "C" fn waiter_thread(runtime: *mut (), _argument: usize) {
    THREAD_TEST_TRACE.store(1, Ordering::Release);
    if !wait_for_event(runtime) || THREAD_TEST_TRACE.load(Ordering::Acquire) != 2 {
        THREAD_TEST_TRACE.store(99, Ordering::Release);
        return;
    }
    THREAD_TEST_TRACE.store(3, Ordering::Release);
    if !sleep_for_ticks(runtime, 2) || THREAD_TEST_TRACE.load(Ordering::Acquire) != 4 {
        THREAD_TEST_TRACE.store(99, Ordering::Release);
        return;
    }
    THREAD_TEST_TRACE.store(5, Ordering::Release);
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-kernel-threads")]
extern "C" fn signaler_thread(runtime: *mut (), _argument: usize) {
    if THREAD_TEST_TRACE.load(Ordering::Acquire) != 1 {
        THREAD_TEST_TRACE.store(99, Ordering::Release);
        return;
    }
    THREAD_TEST_TRACE.store(2, Ordering::Release);
    if !wake_event(runtime) {
        THREAD_TEST_TRACE.store(99, Ordering::Release);
        return;
    }
    yield_current(runtime);
    if THREAD_TEST_TRACE.load(Ordering::Acquire) != 3 {
        THREAD_TEST_TRACE.store(99, Ordering::Release);
        return;
    }
    THREAD_TEST_TRACE.store(4, Ordering::Release);
    while THREAD_TEST_TRACE.load(Ordering::Acquire) != 5 {
        yield_current(runtime);
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-kernel-threads")]
fn wait_for_event(runtime_pointer: *mut ()) -> bool {
    // SAFETY: This is an ordinary cooperative thread, never an IRQ handler.
    unsafe { block_current(runtime_pointer.cast(), None) }
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-kernel-threads")]
fn sleep_for_ticks(runtime_pointer: *mut (), delay: u64) -> bool {
    if delay == 0 {
        return true;
    }
    // SAFETY: The runtime pointer is restored from this thread's initial context;
    // the runtime remains alive until every thread has exited and been reaped.
    unsafe { block_current(runtime_pointer.cast(), Some(delay)) }
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-kernel-threads")]
fn wake_event(runtime_pointer: *mut ()) -> bool {
    let flags = disable_interrupts();
    // SAFETY: IF is clear and only the current cooperative thread mutates policy.
    let result = unsafe {
        let runtime = &mut *runtime_pointer.cast::<KernelThreadRuntime>();
        runtime.policy.wake_one(runtime.event_queue).is_ok()
    };
    restore_interrupts(flags);
    result
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-kernel-threads")]
fn yield_current(runtime_pointer: *mut ()) {
    let flags = disable_interrupts();
    let switch = unsafe {
        let runtime = &mut *runtime_pointer.cast::<KernelThreadRuntime>();
        runtime.poll_wakeups();
        let Some(current) = runtime.policy.current() else {
            restore_interrupts(flags);
            return;
        };
        let old_context = runtime.current_context;
        let next = match runtime.policy.yield_current() {
            Ok(next) => next,
            Err(_) => {
                THREAD_TEST_TRACE.store(99, Ordering::Release);
                restore_interrupts(flags);
                return;
            }
        };
        let next_context = next.slot_index() + 1;
        runtime.current_context = next_context;
        if current == next {
            None
        } else {
            Some((
                core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(runtime.saved_rsp[old_context]),
                runtime.saved_rsp[next_context],
            ))
        }
    };
    if let Some((old_rsp, new_rsp)) = switch {
        // SAFETY: The selected contexts are cooperative same-CPU kernel stacks;
        // temporary references to the scheduler ended before the switch.
        unsafe { rustix_arch_context_switch(old_rsp, new_rsp as *mut usize) };
    }
    restore_interrupts(flags);
}

unsafe fn block_current(runtime_pointer: *mut KernelThreadRuntime, delay: Option<u64>) -> bool {
    let flags = disable_interrupts();
    let switch = {
        // SAFETY: Called from one cooperative thread with IF clear; the state
        // references are scoped entirely before the context switch.
        let runtime = unsafe { &mut *runtime_pointer };
        let input_event = runtime.poll_wakeups();
        if delay.is_none() && runtime.input_events_enabled && input_event {
            restore_interrupts(flags);
            return true;
        }
        let Some(current) = runtime.policy.current() else {
            restore_interrupts(flags);
            return false;
        };
        let slot = current.slot_index();
        let queue = if let Some(delay) = delay {
            let deadline = runtime.ticks.ticks().saturating_add(delay);
            runtime.deadlines[slot] = Some(deadline);
            runtime.timer_queues[slot]
        } else {
            runtime.event_queue
        };
        let next = match runtime.policy.sleep_current(queue) {
            Ok(next) => next,
            Err(_) => {
                runtime.deadlines[slot] = None;
                restore_interrupts(flags);
                return false;
            }
        };
        let next_context = next.map_or(0, |thread| thread.slot_index() + 1);
        let old_context = runtime.current_context;
        runtime.current_context = next_context;
        Some((
            core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(runtime.saved_rsp[old_context]),
            runtime.saved_rsp[next_context],
        ))
    };
    if let Some((old_rsp, new_rsp)) = switch {
        // SAFETY: The current thread is blocked and cannot be selected until a
        // later wake; the target is either a ready thread or the bootstrap stack.
        unsafe { rustix_arch_context_switch(old_rsp, new_rsp as *mut usize) };
    }
    restore_interrupts(flags);
    true
}

unsafe fn exit_current(runtime_pointer: *mut KernelThreadRuntime) -> ! {
    let flags = disable_interrupts();
    let (old_rsp, new_rsp) = {
        // SAFETY: This is the current thread's normal return path, with IF clear.
        let runtime = unsafe { &mut *runtime_pointer };
        runtime.poll_wakeups();
        let old_context = runtime.current_context;
        match runtime.policy.exit_current() {
            Ok(next) => {
                let next_context = next.map_or(0, |thread| thread.slot_index() + 1);
                runtime.current_context = next_context;
                (
                    core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(runtime.saved_rsp[old_context]),
                    runtime.saved_rsp[next_context],
                )
            }
            Err(_) => halt_on_stack_cleanup_failure(),
        }
    };
    // SAFETY: The exited context is never dispatched again; the target is a
    // different ready thread or the retained bootstrap stack.
    unsafe { rustix_arch_context_switch(old_rsp, new_rsp as *mut usize) };
    restore_interrupts(flags);
    halt_on_stack_cleanup_failure()
}

fn disable_interrupts() -> u64 {
    let flags: u64;
    // SAFETY: Bootstrap and cooperative threads execute at CPL 0; RFLAGS is
    // saved before CLI and the stack operation is balanced.
    unsafe { asm!("pushfq", "pop {}", "cli", out(reg) flags) };
    flags
}

fn restore_interrupts(flags: u64) {
    if flags & (1 << 9) != 0 {
        // SAFETY: The caller only restores the prior IF state after its critical
        // section and after the selected stack/context is fully established.
        unsafe { asm!("sti") };
    }
}

unsafe fn rustix_arch_context_switch(old_rsp: *mut usize, new_rsp: *mut usize) {
    // SAFETY: The runtime maintains valid saved stack frames and distinct live
    // contexts; all callers hold IF clear and never switch from interrupt context.
    unsafe { crate::arch::x86_64::context::context_switch(old_rsp, new_rsp) };
}

//! Bounded single-producer/single-consumer input queues for device IRQ paths.
//!
//! Each queue has one producer (its device IRQ handler) and one consumer on the
//! bootstrap CPU. Producers never wait or allocate; full queues drop the newest
//! byte and increment a saturating overflow counter.

use core::sync::atomic::{AtomicU8, AtomicUsize, Ordering};

pub const INPUT_QUEUE_CAPACITY: usize = 256;

pub static UART_INPUT: ByteRing<INPUT_QUEUE_CAPACITY> = ByteRing::new();
pub static KEYBOARD_INPUT: ByteRing<INPUT_QUEUE_CAPACITY> = ByteRing::new();
pub static INPUT_EVENT_PENDING: core::sync::atomic::AtomicBool =
    core::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(false);

/// A fixed-capacity SPSC queue. Its producer and consumer must remain unique.
pub struct ByteRing<const CAPACITY: usize> {
    bytes: [AtomicU8; CAPACITY],
    head: AtomicUsize,
    tail: AtomicUsize,
    head_index: AtomicUsize,
    tail_index: AtomicUsize,
    overflows: AtomicUsize,
}

impl<const CAPACITY: usize> ByteRing<CAPACITY> {
    pub const fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            bytes: [const { AtomicU8::new(0) }; CAPACITY],
            head: AtomicUsize::new(0),
            tail: AtomicUsize::new(0),
            head_index: AtomicUsize::new(0),
            tail_index: AtomicUsize::new(0),
            overflows: AtomicUsize::new(0),
        }
    }

    /// Push without waiting. Returns false when the queue is full.
    pub fn try_push(&self, byte: u8) -> bool {
        if CAPACITY == 0 {
            self.increment_overflows();
            return false;
        }
        let head = self.head.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
        let tail = self.tail.load(Ordering::Acquire);
        if head.wrapping_sub(tail) >= CAPACITY {
            self.increment_overflows();
            return false;
        }
        let index = self.head_index.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
        self.bytes[index].store(byte, Ordering::Relaxed);
        self.head_index
            .store(self.next_index(index), Ordering::Relaxed);
        self.head.store(head.wrapping_add(1), Ordering::Release);
        true
    }

    /// Pop one byte if available; this never waits.
    pub fn try_pop(&self) -> Option<u8> {
        if CAPACITY == 0 {
            return None;
        }
        let tail = self.tail.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
        let head = self.head.load(Ordering::Acquire);
        if tail == head {
            return None;
        }
        let index = self.tail_index.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
        let byte = self.bytes[index].load(Ordering::Relaxed);
        self.tail_index
            .store(self.next_index(index), Ordering::Relaxed);
        self.tail.store(tail.wrapping_add(1), Ordering::Release);
        Some(byte)
    }

    pub fn overflow_count(&self) -> usize {
        self.overflows.load(Ordering::Acquire)
    }

    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.head.load(Ordering::Acquire) == self.tail.load(Ordering::Acquire)
    }

    fn next_index(&self, index: usize) -> usize {
        if index == CAPACITY - 1 {
            0
        } else {
            index + 1
        }
    }

    fn increment_overflows(&self) {
        let _ = self
            .overflows
            .try_update(Ordering::Relaxed, Ordering::Relaxed, |count| {
                Some(count.saturating_add(1))
            });
    }
}

impl<const CAPACITY: usize> Default for ByteRing<CAPACITY> {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::ByteRing;
    use core::assert_eq;

    #[test]
    fn bounded_queue_preserves_order_and_reports_overflow() {
        let queue = ByteRing::<3>::new();
        assert!(queue.is_empty());
        assert!(queue.try_push(b'a'));
        assert!(queue.try_push(b'b'));
        assert!(queue.try_push(b'c'));
        assert!(!queue.try_push(b'd'));
        assert_eq!(queue.overflow_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(queue.try_pop(), Some(b'a'));
        assert!(queue.try_push(b'd'));
        assert_eq!(queue.try_pop(), Some(b'b'));
        assert_eq!(queue.try_pop(), Some(b'c'));
        assert_eq!(queue.try_pop(), Some(b'd'));
        assert_eq!(queue.try_pop(), None);
        assert!(queue.is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn non_power_of_two_capacity_survives_counter_wraparound() {
        let queue = ByteRing::<3>::new();
        queue.head.store(usize::MAX, Ordering::Relaxed);
        queue.tail.store(usize::MAX, Ordering::Relaxed);

        assert!(queue.try_push(b'a'));
        assert!(queue.try_push(b'b'));
        assert!(queue.try_push(b'c'));
        assert_eq!(queue.try_pop(), Some(b'a'));
        assert!(queue.try_push(b'd'));
        assert_eq!(queue.try_pop(), Some(b'b'));
        assert_eq!(queue.try_pop(), Some(b'c'));
        assert_eq!(queue.try_pop(), Some(b'd'));
        assert_eq!(queue.try_pop(), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn zero_capacity_queue_fails_without_dividing_or_waiting() {
        let queue = ByteRing::<0>::new();
        assert!(!queue.try_push(1));
        assert_eq!(queue.try_pop(), None);
        assert_eq!(queue.overflow_count(), 1);
    }
}

//! Bootstrap GDT, TSS, and interrupt entry for x86_64.
//!
//! Bootstrap installs exception and device-IRQ gates with maskable interrupts
//! disabled. APIC setup, route masking, handler registration, and explicit `sti`
//! are owned by the boot path; exceptions remain fatal-only.

use core::arch::{asm, global_asm};
use core::mem::size_of;

const EXCEPTION_COUNT: usize = 32;
const IRQ_FIRST_VECTOR: usize = 0x20;
const IRQ_LAST_VECTOR: usize = 0xef;
const IRQ_VECTOR_COUNT: usize = IRQ_LAST_VECTOR - IRQ_FIRST_VECTOR + 1;
const APIC_SPURIOUS_VECTOR: usize = 0xff;
const IRQ_STUB_COUNT: usize = IRQ_VECTOR_COUNT + 1;
const _: [(); 208] = [(); IRQ_VECTOR_COUNT];
const KERNEL_CODE_SELECTOR: u16 = 0x08;
const STACK_SIZE: usize = 16 * 1024;
const TSS_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE: u64 = 0x89;

#[repr(C, packed)]
struct DescriptorTablePointer {
    limit: u16,
    base: u64,
}

#[repr(C, align(16))]
struct IdtTable([IdtEntry; 256]);

#[repr(C, packed)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct IdtEntry {
    offset_low: u16,
    selector: u16,
    ist: u8,
    attributes: u8,
    offset_middle: u16,
    offset_high: u32,
    reserved: u32,
}

impl IdtEntry {
    const MISSING: Self = Self {
        offset_low: 0,
        selector: 0,
        ist: 0,
        attributes: 0,
        offset_middle: 0,
        offset_high: 0,
        reserved: 0,
    };

    fn interrupt_gate(handler: u64, ist: u8) -> Self {
        Self {
            offset_low: handler as u16,
            selector: KERNEL_CODE_SELECTOR,
            ist: ist & 0x07,
            attributes: 0x8e,
            offset_middle: (handler >> 16) as u16,
            offset_high: (handler >> 32) as u32,
            reserved: 0,
        }
    }
}

#[repr(C, packed)]
struct TaskStateSegment {
    reserved0: u32,
    rsp0: u64,
    rsp1: u64,
    rsp2: u64,
    reserved1: u64,
    ist1: u64,
    ist2: u64,
    ist3: u64,
    ist4: u64,
    ist5: u64,
    ist6: u64,
    ist7: u64,
    reserved2: u64,
    reserved3: u16,
    iomap_base: u16,
}

impl TaskStateSegment {
    const EMPTY: Self = Self {
        reserved0: 0,
        rsp0: 0,
        rsp1: 0,
        rsp2: 0,
        reserved1: 0,
        ist1: 0,
        ist2: 0,
        ist3: 0,
        ist4: 0,
        ist5: 0,
        ist6: 0,
        ist7: 0,
        reserved2: 0,
        reserved3: 0,
        iomap_base: size_of::<Self>() as u16,
    };
}

#[repr(C, align(16))]
struct Stack([u8; STACK_SIZE]);

static mut GDT: [u64; 5] = [0; 5];
static mut IDT: IdtTable = IdtTable([IdtEntry::MISSING; 256]);
static mut TSS: TaskStateSegment = TaskStateSegment::EMPTY;
static mut RING0_STACK: Stack = Stack([0; STACK_SIZE]);
static mut DOUBLE_FAULT_STACK: Stack = Stack([0; STACK_SIZE]);
static mut IRQ_HANDLERS: [Option<IrqHandler>; 256] = [None; 256];

/// A device interrupt callback. The callback is responsible for issuing EOI.
pub type IrqHandler = extern "C" fn();

/// Reasons an IRQ callback could not be registered.
#[allow(dead_code)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum IrqRegistrationError {
    InvalidVector,
    InterruptsEnabled,
    AlreadyRegistered,
}

#[repr(C)]
pub(crate) struct ExceptionContext {
    r15: u64,
    r14: u64,
    r13: u64,
    r12: u64,
    r11: u64,
    r10: u64,
    r9: u64,
    r8: u64,
    rbp: u64,
    rdi: u64,
    rsi: u64,
    rdx: u64,
    rcx: u64,
    rbx: u64,
    rax: u64,
    vector: u64,
    error_code: u64,
    rip: u64,
    cs: u64,
    rflags: u64,
    rsp: u64,
    ss: u64,
}

const _: [(); 16] = [(); size_of::<IdtEntry>()];
const _: [(); 4096] = [(); size_of::<IdtTable>()];
const _: [(); 104] = [(); size_of::<TaskStateSegment>()];
const _: [(); 176] = [(); size_of::<ExceptionContext>()];
const _: [(); 120] = [(); core::mem::offset_of!(ExceptionContext, vector)];
const _: [(); 128] = [(); core::mem::offset_of!(ExceptionContext, error_code)];
const _: [(); 136] = [(); core::mem::offset_of!(ExceptionContext, rip)];
const _: [(); 144] = [(); core::mem::offset_of!(ExceptionContext, cs)];
const _: [(); 152] = [(); core::mem::offset_of!(ExceptionContext, rflags)];
const _: [(); 160] = [(); core::mem::offset_of!(ExceptionContext, rsp)];
const _: [(); 168] = [(); core::mem::offset_of!(ExceptionContext, ss)];

extern "C" {
    static exception_stub_table: [usize; EXCEPTION_COUNT];
    static irq_stub_table: [usize; IRQ_STUB_COUNT];
    fn rustix_load_gdt(descriptor_table_pointer: *const DescriptorTablePointer);
}

/// Install a private kernel GDT/TSS, exception gates, and device IRQ gates.
///
/// The bootstrap runs with maskable interrupts disabled. This routine leaves
/// them disabled and does not modify CR3 or the inherited page-table hierarchy.
pub fn initialize() {
    // SAFETY: Single-core bootstrap ownership; the descriptor tables are private
    // static storage and are initialized before any gate is loaded.
    unsafe {
        asm!("cli", options(nomem, nostack));
        initialize_tss();
        initialize_gdt();
        initialize_idt();
    }
}

unsafe fn initialize_tss() {
    let ring0_stack = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RING0_STACK).cast::<u8>();
    let double_fault_stack = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(DOUBLE_FAULT_STACK).cast::<u8>();
    // SAFETY: These pointers refer to the ends of distinct, aligned static stacks.
    let ring0_top = unsafe { ring0_stack.add(STACK_SIZE) } as u64;
    // SAFETY: These pointers refer to the ends of distinct, aligned static stacks.
    let double_fault_top = unsafe { double_fault_stack.add(STACK_SIZE) } as u64;
    let tss = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(TSS);

    // The architectural TSS fields are packed; use unaligned raw writes rather
    // than creating references to their potentially unaligned storage.
    unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*tss).rsp0).write_unaligned(ring0_top);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*tss).ist1).write_unaligned(double_fault_top);
    }
}

unsafe fn initialize_gdt() {
    let tss_base = core::ptr::addr_of!(TSS) as u64;
    let tss_limit = (size_of::<TaskStateSegment>() - 1) as u64;
    let low = (tss_limit & 0xffff)
        | ((tss_base & 0x00ff_ffff) << 16)
        | (TSS_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE << 40)
        | ((tss_limit & 0x000f_0000) << 32)
        | ((tss_base & 0xff00_0000) << 32);
    let high = tss_base >> 32;

    unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[0]).write(0);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[1]).write(0x00af_9a00_0000_ffff);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[2]).write(0x00cf_9200_0000_ffff);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[3]).write(low);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[4]).write(high);
    }

    let gdtr = DescriptorTablePointer {
        limit: (size_of::<[u64; 5]>() - 1) as u16,
        base: core::ptr::addr_of!(GDT) as u64,
    };
    // SAFETY: `GDT` and its TSS descriptor are initialized and remain live.
    unsafe { rustix_load_gdt(&gdtr) };
}

unsafe fn initialize_idt() {
    let idt_entries = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(IDT.0).cast::<IdtEntry>();
    let stubs = core::ptr::addr_of!(exception_stub_table).cast::<usize>();

    for vector in 0..EXCEPTION_COUNT {
        // SAFETY: The assembly table contains exactly 32 stub addresses.
        let handler = unsafe { stubs.add(vector).read() } as u64;
        let ist = if vector == 8 { 1 } else { 0 };
        // SAFETY: `vector` is bounded by the statically allocated 256-entry IDT.
        unsafe {
            idt_entries
                .add(vector)
                .write(IdtEntry::interrupt_gate(handler, ist));
        }
    }

    let irq_stubs = core::ptr::addr_of!(irq_stub_table).cast::<usize>();
    for vector in IRQ_FIRST_VECTOR..=IRQ_LAST_VECTOR {
        // SAFETY: The assembly table contains one stub for each allocated vector.
        let handler = unsafe { irq_stubs.add(vector - IRQ_FIRST_VECTOR).read() } as u64;
        // SAFETY: `vector` is bounded by the statically allocated 256-entry IDT.
        unsafe {
            idt_entries
                .add(vector)
                .write(IdtEntry::interrupt_gate(handler, 0));
        }
    }
    // SAFETY: The final table entry is the dedicated 0xff spurious-IRQ stub.
    let spurious_handler = unsafe { irq_stubs.add(IRQ_VECTOR_COUNT).read() } as u64;
    // SAFETY: The APIC spurious vector is a valid IDT index.
    unsafe {
        idt_entries
            .add(APIC_SPURIOUS_VECTOR)
            .write(IdtEntry::interrupt_gate(spurious_handler, 0));
    }

    let idtr = DescriptorTablePointer {
        limit: (size_of::<IdtTable>() - 1) as u16,
        base: core::ptr::addr_of!(IDT) as u64,
    };
    // SAFETY: Every architectural exception gate is initialized in static storage.
    unsafe { asm!("lidt [{}]", in(reg) &idtr, options(readonly, nostack, preserves_flags)) };
}

/// Register one callback for an allocated device IRQ vector.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// The caller must keep the IRQ source masked while registering and ensure it
/// is masked whenever this callback is dispatched. The caller must serialize
/// registration against IRQ dispatch on every CPU. `handler` must not allocate,
/// format output, block, or unwind; it runs with IF disabled and owns the EOI.
/// The source must remain masked until all handler state is ready.
#[allow(dead_code)]
pub unsafe fn register_irq_handler(
    vector: u8,
    handler: IrqHandler,
) -> Result<(), IrqRegistrationError> {
    let vector = vector as usize;
    if !(IRQ_FIRST_VECTOR..=IRQ_LAST_VECTOR).contains(&vector) {
        return Err(IrqRegistrationError::InvalidVector);
    }

    let flags: u64;
    // SAFETY: This reads RFLAGS at CPL 0; the temporary push/pop is balanced.
    unsafe {
        asm!("pushfq", "pop {}", out(reg) flags, options(preserves_flags));
    }
    if flags & (1 << 9) != 0 {
        return Err(IrqRegistrationError::InterruptsEnabled);
    }

    // SAFETY: The API contract requires registration to be serialized with IRQ
    // dispatch, and the vector has been checked against the table bounds.
    let slot = unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(IRQ_HANDLERS)
            .cast::<Option<IrqHandler>>()
            .add(vector)
    };
    // SAFETY: `slot` points into the initialized static callback table.
    if unsafe { slot.read() }.is_some() {
        return Err(IrqRegistrationError::AlreadyRegistered);
    }
    // SAFETY: Registration is serialized by the caller's masking/IF contract.
    unsafe { slot.write(Some(handler)) };
    Ok(())
}

/// Device IRQ target called by the normalized assembly stubs.
#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn rustix_irq_dispatch(vector: u64) {
    if vector == APIC_SPURIOUS_VECTOR as u64 {
        return;
    }

    if !(IRQ_FIRST_VECTOR as u64..=IRQ_LAST_VECTOR as u64).contains(&vector) {
        fatal_irq_halt();
    }

    // SAFETY: Interrupt gates clear IF, and registration's safety contract
    // serializes writes against this read. No mutable reference is created.
    let handler = unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of!(IRQ_HANDLERS)
            .cast::<Option<IrqHandler>>()
            .add(vector as usize)
            .read()
    };
    match handler {
        Some(handler) => handler(),
        None => fatal_irq_halt(),
    }
}

fn fatal_irq_halt() -> ! {
    loop {
        // SAFETY: Unknown device interrupts are fatal and must not be retried.
        unsafe { asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    }
}

/// Fatal exception target called by the assembly stubs.
#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn rustix_exception_dispatch(context: *const ExceptionContext) -> ! {
    // SAFETY: The common assembly stub passes a pointer to its normalized stack
    // frame, which remains live for the duration of this non-returning handler.
    let context = unsafe { &*context };
    crate::kprintln!(
        "KERNEL EXCEPTION: vector {} ({}) error={:#018x} RIP={:#018x}",
        context.vector,
        exception_name(context.vector),
        context.error_code,
        context.rip
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "CS={:#06x} SS={:#06x} RFLAGS={:#018x} RSP={:#018x}",
        context.cs,
        context.ss,
        context.rflags,
        context.rsp
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "RAX={:#018x} RBX={:#018x} RCX={:#018x}",
        context.rax,
        context.rbx,
        context.rcx
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "RDX={:#018x} RSI={:#018x} RDI={:#018x} RBP={:#018x}",
        context.rdx,
        context.rsi,
        context.rdi,
        context.rbp
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "R8={:#018x} R9={:#018x} R10={:#018x} R11={:#018x}",
        context.r8,
        context.r9,
        context.r10,
        context.r11
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "R12={:#018x} R13={:#018x} R14={:#018x} R15={:#018x}",
        context.r12,
        context.r13,
        context.r14,
        context.r15
    );

    if context.vector == 14 {
        crate::kprintln!(
            "page fault: present={} write={} user={} reserved={} instruction-fetch={}",
            context.error_code & 1 != 0,
            context.error_code & 2 != 0,
            context.error_code & 4 != 0,
            context.error_code & 8 != 0,
            context.error_code & 16 != 0
        );
        let fault_address: u64;
        // SAFETY: Reading CR2 is a privileged x86_64 operation in this handler.
        unsafe {
            asm!("mov {}, cr2", out(reg) fault_address, options(nomem, nostack, preserves_flags))
        };
        crate::kprintln!("page fault address (CR2): {:#018x}", fault_address);
    }

    loop {
        // SAFETY: Fatal exceptions are not recoverable in the current kernel.
        unsafe { asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    }
}

fn exception_name(vector: u64) -> &'static str {
    match vector {
        0 => "divide error",
        1 => "debug",
        2 => "non-maskable interrupt",
        3 => "breakpoint",
        4 => "overflow",
        5 => "bound range",
        6 => "invalid opcode",
        7 => "device not available",
        8 => "double fault",
        9 => "coprocessor segment overrun",
        10 => "invalid TSS",
        11 => "segment not present",
        12 => "stack-segment fault",
        13 => "general protection fault",
        14 => "page fault",
        16 => "x87 floating-point",
        17 => "alignment check",
        18 => "machine check",
        19 => "SIMD floating-point",
        20 => "virtualization",
        21 => "control protection",
        28 => "hypervisor injection",
        29 => "VMM communication",
        30 => "security exception",
        _ => "reserved or architecture-specific exception",
    }
}

//! Kernel-side Crabshell frontend: serial input, prompts, and RAM-filesystem commands.

use crabshell::{parse, Command, ParseError, MAX_LINE_LENGTH};
use rustix_kernel::vfs::{EntryKind, FsError, RamFs, MAX_PATH_CAPACITY};

use crate::arch::x86_64::serial;
use rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator;
use rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap;

/// Run Crabshell forever on the bootstrap CPU.
pub fn run(
    filesystem: &mut RamFs,
    mut cwd: usize,
    memory_map: &MemoryMap,
    frame_allocator: *const FrameAllocator,
    runtime: *mut (),
) -> ! {
    crate::kprintln!("crabshell: ready (volatile RAM filesystem)");
    print_motd(filesystem, cwd);

    let mut input = [0u8; MAX_LINE_LENGTH];
    let mut reported_input_wait = false;
    loop {
        print_prompt(filesystem, cwd);
        let length = read_line(
            &mut input,
            filesystem,
            cwd,
            runtime,
            &mut reported_input_wait,
        );
        if length == 0 {
            continue;
        }

        let line = match core::str::from_utf8(&input[..length]) {
            Ok(line) => line,
            Err(_) => {
                crate::kprintln!("crabshell: input must be valid UTF-8");
                continue;
            }
        };

        match parse(line) {
            Ok(Some(command)) => {
                execute(command, filesystem, &mut cwd, memory_map, frame_allocator)
            }
            Ok(None) => {}
            Err(error) => print_parse_error(error),
        }
    }
}

fn print_prompt(filesystem: &RamFs, cwd: usize) {
    let mut path = [0u8; MAX_PATH_CAPACITY];
    match filesystem.write_path(cwd, &mut path) {
        Ok(length) => match core::str::from_utf8(&path[..length]) {
            Ok(path) => serial::print(format_args!("root@rustix:{}# ", path)),
            Err(_) => serial::print(format_args!("root@rustix:/?# ")),
        },
        Err(_) => serial::print(format_args!("root@rustix:/?# ")),
    }
}

fn read_line(
    input: &mut [u8; MAX_LINE_LENGTH],
    filesystem: &RamFs,
    cwd: usize,
    runtime: *mut (),
    reported_input_wait: &mut bool,
) -> usize {
    let mut length = 0;
    loop {
        let byte = match serial::try_read_byte() {
            Some(byte) => byte,
            None => {
                if let Some(scancode) = crate::arch::x86_64::keyboard::try_read_irq_scancode() {
                    if scancode == 0xe0 || scancode & 0x80 == 0 {
                        serial::print(format_args!(
                            "\r\nPS/2 raw scancode IRQ: {:#04x}\r\n",
                            scancode
                        ));
                        print_prompt(filesystem, cwd);
                        for &byte in &input[..length] {
                            serial::print(format_args!("{}", byte as char));
                        }
                    }
                    continue;
                }
                if runtime.is_null() {
                    core::hint::spin_loop();
                } else {
                    if !*reported_input_wait {
                        crate::kprintln!("kernel shell thread runtime: cooperative input wait");
                        *reported_input_wait = true;
                    }
                    crate::kernel_threads::wait_for_input(runtime);
                }
                continue;
            }
        };

        match byte {
            b'\r' | b'\n' => {
                crate::kprintln!();
                return length;
            }
            0x03 => {
                crate::kprintln!("^C");
                return 0;
            }
            0x08 | 0x7f if length > 0 => {
                length -= 1;
                serial::print(format_args!("\x08 \x08"));
            }
            0x20..=0x7e if length < input.len() => {
                input[length] = byte;
                length += 1;
                serial::print(format_args!("{}", byte as char));
            }
            0x20..=0x7e => serial::print(format_args!("\x07")),
            _ => {}
        }
    }
}

fn execute(
    command: Command<'_>,
    filesystem: &mut RamFs,
    cwd: &mut usize,
    memory_map: &MemoryMap,
    frame_allocator: *const FrameAllocator,
) {
    match command {
        Command::Help => print_help(),
        Command::Clear => serial::print(format_args!("\x1b[2J\x1b[H")),
        Command::Pwd => {
            let mut path = [0u8; MAX_PATH_CAPACITY];
            match filesystem.write_path(*cwd, &mut path) {
                Ok(length) => match core::str::from_utf8(&path[..length]) {
                    Ok(path) => crate::kprintln!("{}", path),
                    Err(_) => crate::kprintln!("crabshell: could not display current path"),
                },
                Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
            }
        }
        Command::Meminfo => {
            // SAFETY: The sole shell thread reads frame counts on the bootstrap
            // CPU; the allocator is never mutated from an IRQ or another thread.
            let allocator = unsafe { &*frame_allocator };
            let managed = allocator.managed_frames();
            let free = allocator.free_frames();
            crate::kprintln!("usable RAM: {} bytes", memory_map.usable_bytes());
            crate::kprintln!(
                "physical frames: {} managed, {} free, {} allocated",
                managed,
                free,
                managed - free
            );
        }
        Command::Ls(path) => {
            let directory = match path {
                Some(path) => match filesystem.resolve(*cwd, path) {
                    Ok(node) => node,
                    Err(error) => {
                        report_fs_error(error);
                        return;
                    }
                },
                None => *cwd,
            };
            list_directory(filesystem, directory);
        }
        Command::Cd(path) => match filesystem.resolve(*cwd, path) {
            Ok(node) => match filesystem.kind(node) {
                Ok(EntryKind::Directory) => *cwd = node,
                Ok(EntryKind::File) => report_fs_error(FsError::NotDirectory),
                Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
            },
            Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
        },
        Command::Mkdir(path) => match filesystem.create_dir_path(*cwd, path) {
            Ok(_) => {}
            Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
        },
        Command::Touch(path) => match filesystem.open_or_create_file(*cwd, path) {
            Ok(_) => {}
            Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
        },
        Command::Write { path, contents } => {
            if let Err(error) = filesystem.write_file_path(*cwd, path, contents.as_bytes()) {
                report_fs_error(error);
            }
        }
        Command::Append { path, contents } => {
            if let Err(error) = filesystem.append_file_path(*cwd, path, contents.as_bytes()) {
                report_fs_error(error);
            }
        }
        Command::Cp {
            source,
            destination,
        } => match filesystem.copy_file_path(*cwd, source, destination) {
            Ok(()) => {}
            Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
        },
        Command::Mv {
            source,
            destination,
        } => match filesystem.move_file_path(*cwd, source, destination) {
            Ok(()) => {}
            Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
        },
        Command::Cat(path) => match filesystem.resolve(*cwd, path) {
            Ok(node) => match filesystem.read_file(node) {
                Ok(bytes) => match core::str::from_utf8(bytes) {
                    Ok(text) => print_file_contents(text),
                    Err(_) => crate::kprintln!("crabshell: binary file display is not supported"),
                },
                Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
            },
            Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
        },
        Command::Rm(path) => match filesystem.remove_file_path(*cwd, path) {
            Ok(()) => {}
            Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
        },
        Command::Rmdir(path) => match filesystem.resolve(*cwd, path) {
            Ok(node) if node == *cwd => {
                crate::kprintln!("crabshell: cannot remove the current directory");
            }
            Ok(node) => match filesystem.remove_dir(node) {
                Ok(()) => {}
                Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
            },
            Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
        },
    }
}

fn list_directory(filesystem: &RamFs, directory: usize) {
    match filesystem.kind(directory) {
        Ok(EntryKind::File) => match filesystem.entry(directory) {
            Ok(entry) => crate::kprintln!("{} ({} bytes)", entry.name, entry.size),
            Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
        },
        Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
        Ok(EntryKind::Directory) => match filesystem.child_count(directory) {
            Ok(0) => crate::kprintln!("(empty)"),
            Ok(count) => {
                for index in 0..count {
                    let Some(entry) = filesystem.child_at(directory, index) else {
                        crate::kprintln!("crabshell: directory changed while listing");
                        return;
                    };
                    match entry.kind {
                        EntryKind::Directory => crate::kprintln!("{}/", entry.name),
                        EntryKind::File => {
                            crate::kprintln!("{}  {} bytes", entry.name, entry.size)
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
            Err(error) => report_fs_error(error),
        },
    }
}

fn print_file_contents(text: &str) {
    for (index, line) in text.split('\n').enumerate() {
        if index != 0 {
            serial::print(format_args!("\r\n"));
        }
        serial::print(format_args!("{}", line.strip_suffix('\r').unwrap_or(line)));
    }
    if !text.ends_with('\n') {
        crate::kprintln!();
    }
}

fn print_motd(filesystem: &RamFs, cwd: usize) {
    if let Ok(node) = filesystem.resolve(cwd, "/etc/motd") {
        if let Ok(bytes) = filesystem.read_file(node) {
            if let Ok(text) = core::str::from_utf8(bytes) {
                print_file_contents(text);
            }
        }
    }
}

fn print_help() {
    crate::kprintln!("Crabshell commands:");
    crate::kprintln!("  help                 show this help");
    crate::kprintln!("  clear                clear an ANSI-compatible terminal");
    crate::kprintln!("  pwd                  print the current directory");
    crate::kprintln!("  meminfo              show validated memory and frame counts");
    crate::kprintln!("  ls [PATH]            list a directory or file");
    crate::kprintln!("  cd PATH              change the current directory");
    crate::kprintln!("  mkdir PATH            create a directory");
    crate::kprintln!("  touch PATH            create an empty file");
    crate::kprintln!("  write PATH TEXT       replace a file's contents");
    crate::kprintln!("  append PATH TEXT      append text to a file");
    crate::kprintln!("  cp SOURCE DEST        copy a file, replacing DEST if it exists");
    crate::kprintln!("  mv SOURCE DEST        move/rename; refuse existing DEST");
    crate::kprintln!("  cat PATH              print a text file");
    crate::kprintln!("  rm PATH               remove a file");
    crate::kprintln!("  rmdir PATH            remove an empty directory");
    crate::kprintln!("  write/append accept a quoted or unquoted text remainder.");
    crate::kprintln!("  RAM filesystem: 31 entries plus root; files up to 1024 bytes.");
}

fn print_parse_error(error: ParseError) {
    match error {
        ParseError::UnknownCommand => crate::kprintln!("crabshell: unknown command (try 'help')"),
        ParseError::MissingArgument => crate::kprintln!("crabshell: missing path argument"),
        ParseError::MissingText => {
            crate::kprintln!("crabshell: missing text (usage: write PATH TEXT)")
        }
        ParseError::TooManyArguments => crate::kprintln!("crabshell: too many arguments"),
        ParseError::UnterminatedQuote => crate::kprintln!("crabshell: unterminated text quote"),
    }
}

fn report_fs_error(error: FsError) {
    let message = match error {
        FsError::InvalidPath => "invalid path",
        FsError::InvalidName => "invalid file name",
        FsError::NameTooLong => "file name is too long (maximum 31 UTF-8 bytes)",
        FsError::AlreadyExists => "an entry with that name already exists",
        FsError::NotFound => "path not found",
        FsError::NotDirectory => "a path component is not a directory",
        FsError::IsDirectory => "operation requires a file, not a directory",
        FsError::DirectoryNotEmpty => "directory is not empty",
        FsError::NoSpace => "RAM filesystem is full",
        FsError::FileTooLarge => "file exceeds the 1024-byte limit",
        FsError::RootOperation => "operation is not permitted on the root directory",
        FsError::BufferTooSmall => "path exceeds the display buffer",
    };
    crate::kprintln!("crabshell: {}", message);
}

struct LimineHhdmPageTableReader<'a> {
    memory_map: &'a rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
}

impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader for LimineHhdmPageTableReader<'_> {
    type Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError;

    fn read_entry(&self, table_physical: u64, index: u16) -> Result<u64, Self::Error> {
        if index >= 512 {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::InvalidHhdmRange);
        }
        let table_end = table_physical
            .checked_add(rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        if !self.memory_map.range_is_within_region_kind(
            table_physical,
            table_end,
            rustix_kernel::memory::RegionKind::BootloaderReclaimable,
        ) {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::NotLimineMapped);
        }
        let table_address = self.memory_map.limine_hhdm_address(
            self.hhdm_offset,
            table_physical,
            rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
            Some(self.physical_address_bits),
            self.virtual_address_bits,
        )?;
        let entry_address = table_address
            .checked_add(u64::from(index) * core::mem::size_of::<u64>() as u64)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        // SAFETY: The complete table page was restricted to bootloader-reclaimable
        // memory and its HHDM address arithmetic was checked. The reader relies
        // on the Limine base-revision-3 mapping contract and never returns a ref.
        Ok(unsafe { (entry_address as *const u64).read_volatile() })
    }
}

struct LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'a> {
    memory_map: &'a rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
}

// SAFETY: `prepare_table` accepts only an allocator-issued frame and validates
// its complete usable span and HHDM address. Handles are only used while the
// candidate retains the frame token and this unique backend borrow.
unsafe impl rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTableMemory for LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'_> {
    type PreparedTable = u64;
    type Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError;

    fn prepare_table(
        &mut self,
        frame: &rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
    ) -> Result<Self::PreparedTable, Self::Error> {
        frame.hhdm_address(
            self.memory_map,
            self.hhdm_offset,
            Some(self.physical_address_bits),
            self.virtual_address_bits,
        )
    }

    unsafe fn read_entry(
        &self,
        table: Self::PreparedTable,
        index: u16,
    ) -> Result<u64, Self::Error> {
        if index >= 512 {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::InvalidHhdmRange);
        }
        let entry_address = table
            .checked_add(u64::from(index) * core::mem::size_of::<u64>() as u64)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        // SAFETY: The unsafe trait contract requires `table` to be the prepared
        // HHDM address of a complete writable frame; the index is in [0, 512).
        Ok(unsafe { (entry_address as *const u64).read_volatile() })
    }

    unsafe fn clear_table(&mut self, table: Self::PreparedTable) {
        let entries = table as *mut u64;
        // SAFETY: The caller provides a handle prepared by this backend for a
        // complete writable frame retained by its candidate.
        unsafe {
            for index in 0..512 {
                entries.add(index).write_volatile(0);
            }
        }
    }

    unsafe fn write_entry(&mut self, table: Self::PreparedTable, index: u16, value: u64) {
        if index >= 512 {
            return;
        }
        let entry = (table as *mut u64).wrapping_add(usize::from(index));
        // SAFETY: The caller provides a prepared complete frame and an index in
        // range; this writes one entry without creating a Rust reference.
        unsafe { entry.write_volatile(value) };

    unsafe fn invalidate_page(&mut self, virtual_address: u64) {

        // at CPL 0 with exclusive local page-table ownership.
        unsafe {
            core::arch::asm!(
                "invlpg [{}]",
                in(reg) virtual_address,
                options(nostack, preserves_flags)
            );
        }
    }

struct KernelHeapMappingContext {
    candidate: *mut (),
    allocator: *mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    cpu_info: *const arch::x86_64::cpu::CpuInfo,
}

unsafe fn map_kernel_heap_pages(
    opaque_context: *mut (),
    first_page: usize,
    page_count: usize,
) -> bool {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{
        validate_mapping_range, CachePolicy, CandidatePageTables, EffectiveMemoryType, MtrrState,
        PagePermissions, PatLayout, PAGE_SIZE,
    };

    if page_count == 0
        || first_page
            .checked_add(page_count)
            .is_none_or(|end| end > KERNEL_HEAP_GROWTH_MAX_PAGES)
    {
        return false;
    }

    // SAFETY: The caller configures this callback only after the active root,
    // allocator, CPU snapshot, and local context are all live. The boot path is
    // single-vCPU and never returns from the stack containing that context.
    let state = unsafe { &mut *opaque_context.cast::<KernelHeapMappingContext>() };
    // SAFETY: These pointers refer to the retained local candidate and BootInfo
    // members. The callback is synchronous and never stores a derived reference.
    let candidate = unsafe {
        &mut *state
            .candidate
            .cast::<CandidatePageTables<'static, LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'static>>>()
    };
    // SAFETY: The frame allocator and CPU snapshot remain owned by retained
    // BootInfo; this callback runs on the sole CPU with the heap lock held.
    let allocator = unsafe { &mut *state.allocator };
    // SAFETY: The CPU snapshot is immutable and remains live with BootInfo.
    let cpu_info = unsafe { &*state.cpu_info };

    let flags: u64;
    // SAFETY: The callback runs at CPL 0; save IF before disabling local IRQs
    // while the active page tables and allocator are mutated.
    unsafe { core::arch::asm!("pushfq", "pop {}", "cli", out(reg) flags) };
    let result = (|| {
        let physical_width = cpu_info.physical_address_bits?;
        let pat = PatLayout::from_msr_value(cpu_info.pat_msr_value?).ok()?;
        let mtrrs = match &cpu_info.mtrr {
            MtrrState::Captured(registers) => registers.validated_layout(physical_width).ok()?,
            _ => return None,
        };
        let permissions = PagePermissions {
            writable: true,
            executable: false,
            user_accessible: false,
        };
        let mut mapped = 0usize;
        for page in first_page..first_page + page_count {
            let virtual_address = KERNEL_HEAP_GROWTH_VIRTUAL_BASE
                .checked_add((page as u64).checked_mul(PAGE_SIZE)?)?;
            let frame = match allocator.allocate() {
                Some(frame) => frame,
                None => {
                    rollback_kernel_heap_pages(candidate, allocator, first_page, mapped);
                    return None;
                }
            };
            let mapping = match validate_mapping_range(
                virtual_address,
                frame.address(),
                PAGE_SIZE,
                permissions,
                Some(physical_width),
                cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
            ) {
                Ok(mapping) => mapping,
                Err(_) => {
                    deallocate_kernel_heap_frame(allocator, frame);
                    rollback_kernel_heap_pages(candidate, allocator, first_page, mapped);
                    return None;
                }
            };
            let attributes = match mapping.select_cache_attributes(
                CachePolicy::WriteBack,
                pat,
                &mtrrs,
                cpu_info.normal_caching,
            ) {
                Ok(attributes) if attributes.effective_type() == EffectiveMemoryType::WriteBack => {
                    attributes
                }
                _ => {
                    deallocate_kernel_heap_frame(allocator, frame);
                    rollback_kernel_heap_pages(candidate, allocator, first_page, mapped);
                    return None;
                }
            };
            // SAFETY: IF is clear, the current candidate owns the active root,
            // and the allocator-issued frame is mapped RW/NX with local TLB
            // invalidation before its token becomes page-table-owned.
            if let Err(failure) =
                unsafe { candidate.map_owned_page_active(allocator, frame, mapping, attributes) }
            {
                deallocate_kernel_heap_frame(allocator, failure.frame);
                rollback_kernel_heap_pages(candidate, allocator, first_page, mapped);
                return None;
            }
            mapped += 1;
        }
        Some(())
    })()
    .is_some();
    if flags & (1 << 9) != 0 {
        // SAFETY: The mapping transaction is complete or fully rolled back.
        unsafe { core::arch::asm!("sti") };
    }
    result
}

fn rollback_kernel_heap_pages(
    candidate: &mut rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTables<
        'static,
        LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'static>,
    >,
    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    first_page: usize,
    mapped_pages: usize,
) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE;

    for page in (first_page..first_page + mapped_pages).rev() {
        let virtual_address = KERNEL_HEAP_GROWTH_VIRTUAL_BASE + page as u64 * PAGE_SIZE;
        // SAFETY: The pages belong to this transaction in the current active
        // root; unmapping invalidates their TLB entries before token return.
        let frame = unsafe { candidate.unmap_owned_page_active(virtual_address) }
            .unwrap_or_else(|_| halt_forever());
        deallocate_kernel_heap_frame(allocator, frame);
    }
}

fn deallocate_kernel_heap_frame(
    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    frame: rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
) {
    if allocator.deallocate(frame).is_err() {
        halt_forever();
    }
}

    },
    InvalidMapping(rustix_kernel::paging::MappingError),
    CandidateMap(

struct CandidateAcpiReader<'candidate, 'memory, 'map> {

// The legacy-reserved authorization is accepted only for RSDP reads; all

impl CandidateAcpiReader<'_, '_, '_> {
    fn read_mapped(
        &mut self,
        physical_start: u64,
        output: &mut [u8],
        allow_legacy_rsdp: bool,
    ) -> Result<(), AcpiMappingError> {
        use rustix_kernel::paging::{
            validate_mapping_range, CachePolicy, PagePermissions, PageWalkOutcome, PAGE_SIZE,
        };

        if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != self.previous_cr3 {

                physical_start,
                length,

            self.memory_map.validate_acpi_span(
                physical_start,
                length,

        }
        .map_err(|error| AcpiMappingError::InvalidAcpiSpan {
            physical_start,
            length: output.len(),

        let permissions = PagePermissions {
            writable: false,
            executable: false,
            user_accessible: false,

        let mut copied = 0usize;
        while copied < output.len() {
            let current_physical = physical_start.checked_add(copied as u64).ok_or(
                AcpiMappingError::InvalidAcpiSpan {

                    length: output.len(),
                    error: rustix_kernel::memory::AcpiSpanError::AddressOverflow,

            )?;

            let page_offset = current_physical - physical_page;
            let page_length = (PAGE_SIZE - page_offset).min((output.len() - copied) as u64);
            let mapping = validate_mapping_range(
                self.virtual_address,
                physical_page,
                PAGE_SIZE,
                permissions,
                Some(self.physical_address_bits),
                self.virtual_address_bits,
            )
            .map_err(AcpiMappingError::InvalidMapping)?;
            let cache_attributes = mapping
                .select_cache_attributes(
                    CachePolicy::Uncacheable,
                    self.pat,
                    &self.cache_layout,
                    self.normal_caching,
                )
                .map_err(AcpiMappingError::InvalidMapping)?;
            self.candidate
                .map_acpi_page(self.allocator, span, mapping, cache_attributes)
                .map_err(|failure| AcpiMappingError::CandidateMap(failure.cause))?;

            let candidate_mapping_is_valid = matches!(
                self.candidate.walk(self.virtual_address),
                Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation))
                    if translation.physical_address == physical_page
                        && translation.permissions == permissions
            );
            if !candidate_mapping_is_valid {
                self.remove_temporary_mapping();
                return Err(AcpiMappingError::CandidateWalk);
            }
            if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != self.previous_cr3 {
                halt_forever();
            }

            // SAFETY: The candidate is a complete clone of the current inherited
            // hierarchy with all critical paths verified; this temporary page is
            // supervisor R/NX and the candidate remains owned by this stack.
            unsafe { arch::x86_64::cpu::write_cr3_with_global_flush(self.candidate_cr3) };
            // SAFETY: The CR3 write above installed the candidate root and maskable
            // interrupts remain disabled during this single-core bootstrap read.
            unsafe { self.candidate.mark_active() };
            if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != self.candidate_cr3 {
                // SAFETY: Restoring the previous validated root preserves all code,
                // stack, data, and exception mappings needed by this path.
                unsafe { arch::x86_64::cpu::write_cr3_with_global_flush(self.previous_cr3) };
                if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != self.previous_cr3 {
                    halt_forever();
                }
                // SAFETY: The verified CR3 is no longer the candidate root.
                unsafe { self.candidate.mark_inactive() };
                self.remove_temporary_mapping();
                return Err(AcpiMappingError::UnexpectedCurrentCr3);
            }

            let source = (self.virtual_address + page_offset) as *const u8;
            for offset in 0..page_length as usize {
                // SAFETY: The exact physical page is temporarily mapped R/NX in
                // the active candidate and this byte lies within its 4 KiB leaf.
                output[copied + offset] = unsafe { source.add(offset).read_volatile() };
            }

            // SAFETY: The prior root remains allocated and its critical mappings
            // were verified before this temporary switch.
            unsafe { arch::x86_64::cpu::write_cr3_with_global_flush(self.previous_cr3) };
            if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != self.previous_cr3 {
                halt_forever();
            }
            // SAFETY: The previous root was restored and verified above.
            unsafe { self.candidate.mark_inactive() };
            self.remove_temporary_mapping();
            copied += page_length as usize;
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

// SAFETY: `read_mapped` authorizes ordinary table reads only through validated
// ACPI map regions; its separate RSDP entry point permits only the bounded legacy
// reserved window recognized by `MemoryMap::validate_rsdp_span`.
unsafe impl rustix_kernel::acpi::AcpiPhysicalReader for CandidateAcpiReader<'_, '_, '_> {
    type Error = AcpiMappingError;

    fn read(&mut self, physical_start: u64, output: &mut [u8]) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
        self.read_mapped(physical_start, output, false)
    }

    fn read_rsdp(&mut self, physical_start: u64, output: &mut [u8]) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
        self.read_mapped(physical_start, output, true)
    }
}

// Capture Limine's entry RSP before a Rust prologue changes it. The synthetic
// return slot is part of the SysV entry stack; realign before calling Rust.
core::arch::global_asm!(
    ".section .text",
    ".code64",
    ".global _start",
    ".type _start, @function",
    "_start:",
    "mov rdi, rsp",
    "and rsp, -16",
    "call rustix_start",
    "ud2",
    ".size _start, . - _start",
);

#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn rustix_start(entry_rsp: u64) -> ! {
    arch::x86_64::serial::initialize();
    kprintln!("Rustix kernel: x86_64 Rust bootstrap");
    arch::x86_64::interrupts::initialize();
    kprintln!("x86_64 exception diagnostics: enabled (IRQs remain disabled)");
    let mut boot_info = match boot::capture_boot_information(entry_rsp) {
        Ok(boot_info) => boot_info,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("boot information rejected: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    boot::report_boot_information(&boot_info);

    #[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
    probe_hhdm_frame(&mut boot_info);

    #[cfg(any(feature = "inject-page-fault", feature = "inject-invalid-opcode"))]
    run_fault_injection();

    activate_cloned_page_tables_and_run(&mut boot_info)
}

fn activate_cloned_page_tables_and_run(boot_info: &mut boot::BootInfo) -> ! {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{
        encode_cr3_value, CandidatePageTables, PageWalkConfig, PageWalkOutcome, PAGE_SIZE,
    };

    let physical_address_bits = match boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits {
        Some(bits) => bits,
        None => {
