# Testing and verification

## Current checks

`just verify` runs the standard development verification sequence:

1. `just fmt` — fail on formatting differences across the workspace.
2. `just test` — run host-side ACPI parser/traversal, borrowed-page mapping, IRQ vector allocator, PIT rate/time arithmetic, SPSC input-queue wraparound, scheduler, memory-map, mapping-range/PTE-bit policy, frame-allocator, heap, RAM-filesystem, and Crabshell parser tests.
3. `just check` — check the `x86_64-unknown-none` kernel target.
4. `just smoke` — build the pinned hybrid ISO, boot it in QEMU's default BIOS mode, and check that Crabshell reaches its prompt within a deadline.
5. `just uefi-smoke` — boot the same ISO with OVMF and require the copied MADT report, CR3/page-table transition and TLB-flush markers, timer IRQ delivery/EOI, and shell prompt within a deadline.
6. `just active-map-smoke` and `just thread-smoke` — exercise active owned-page mapping/TLB invalidation and (under OVMF) IRQ-save lock IF restoration, cooperative event/wait behavior, timer preemption of non-yielding workers, x87/SSE state preservation, timed sleep while another ready thread repeatedly yields, guarded stacks, and frame-backed heap growth; both restore the default image.
7. `just input-smoke` — under OVMF, type a partial `pwd` over UART, inject ordinary and extended PS/2 scancodes through QMP, require each diagnostic to redraw the prompt and partial line, then finish the command and verify its output. The QMP socket is created under the host temporary directory because WSL `/mnt/c` does not support Unix sockets.

`just frame-smoke` builds an opt-in kernel variant that allocates one `Usable` frame, validates its HHDM address, writes and reads the whole page, clears it, returns it, and checks the prompt in QEMU. It reads the inherited root, walks all pages in the kernel image segments and requested 256 KiB stack span, compares effective PAT/MTRR types for kernel-image/HHDM aliases, and exercises a separate candidate map/unmap/release. The normal boot path in this image also clones the full reachable inherited hierarchy, hardens kernel-image HHDM aliases to text/rodata R/NX and data RW/NX while retaining PAT bits, switches CR3 with active-PCID and global-TLB invalidation, verifies the active root and critical mappings, and exercises the global heap's alignment, reuse, and deterministic exhaustion. The smoke test requires a serial marker confirming the applicable TLB invalidation path. The workflow restores the default release kernel and ISO. These probes rely on Limine's HHDM contract and do not inventory every unrelated mapping or prove physical-hardware correctness. `just fault-smoke` separately builds opt-in kernel variants that deliberately trigger a page fault and an invalid opcode. It requires each QEMU run to report the expected exception (and CR2 for the page fault), avoid the shell prompt, and remain halted until timeout. It then rebuilds and restores the default release kernel and ISO. These are fatal-path diagnostics, not exception recovery tests; diagnostic Cargo features are disabled by default and mutually exclusive.

Keep the ACPI parser, IRQ vector allocator, PIT time arithmetic, Crabshell parser, VFS, memory-map validator, paging policy helpers, frame allocator, and fixed heap independent of hardware so ACPI signatures/checksums/MADT bounds and ACPI page-rounded span authorization, IRQ vector ownership/exhaustion, PIT divisor and elapsed-time arithmetic, syntax, path handling, address and leaf-PTE bit policy, PAT/MTRR policy, storage semantics, frame ownership, HHDM/root-range calculations, allocation alignment, reuse, and exhaustion can be tested without booting. Pure tests validate captured MTRR register snapshots, resolve the Intel SDM Table 11-7 PAT/MTRR combinations for one physical address, select a PAT index that remains uniform across MTRR boundaries in an aligned range, bind that selection to validated mapping metadata before encoding leaves, and walk synthetic four-/five-level page tables including large-page leaves. Host tests also exercise the candidate builder's owned-table walk, clone ownership, 4-/5-level mapping, 2 MiB/1 GiB splitting, permission/cache-bit preservation, active-state mutation/release guard, transactional allocation/prepare rollback, and retryable frame-release failure. Heap tests cover alignment, exact-layout free/reuse, zero-sized rejection, metadata exhaustion, and arena exhaustion. Tests reject malformed state, unsupported discontinuous masks, invalid indexes/ranges, out-of-range addresses, mismatched physical widths, and non-normal caching mode. The pure inherited-table walker does not access hardware tables; the opt-in QEMU reader and candidate backend use checked HHDM addresses. Boot-time QEMU checks a subset of live kernel/HHDM aliases but does not inventory all aliases or prove complete transition safety. Boot separately captures the registers and CR0 caching mode read-only and reports a diagnostic resolution; this is not a page-table or mapping test. The GDT/TSS/IDT and CPU-register paths are privileged kernel code. The temporary ACPI CR3/map/copy/restore path is hardware-only. The 2026-11-07 WSL2 q35 smoke reached the shell but rejected the MADT table span as `NotFullyAcpiBacked`; it did not validate a successful ACPI physical read or CR3 round-trip. QEMU boot and fault-injection checks complement, but do not replace, static review and target builds. Add tests for boundaries and failure behavior when introducing new pure kernel helpers. The kernel binary is not a host test target.

`just uefi-smoke` locates combined OVMF firmware or a matching CODE/VARS pair in standard system directories. `just thread-smoke` uses an opt-in kernel-thread probe, requires the lock-state, cooperative scheduling, non-yielding timer-preemption, and FPU-preservation markers, and restores the default release image. Split firmware uses a fresh temporary copy of the VARS template. `just input-smoke` validates UART RX and PS/2 IRQ delivery/wakeup against the normal default kernel. The OVMF checks require the expected MADT report and CR3-transition markers; install the Ubuntu `ovmf` package if no firmware is found. The BIOS smoke remains separate: if firmware places the RSDT in Reserved memory, the kernel's ACPI validation is expected to fail closed rather than accepting that table span.

## What current checks do not prove

- `cargo check` does not perform a final target link.
- A successful ELF link does not prove the boot protocol is recognized or `_start` is reached.
- Host unit tests do not validate privileged instructions, UART behavior, memory-map pointer validity, page tables, interrupts, or actual hardware. The QEMU boot path exercises the gated EFER/PAT reads and bounded MTRR capture and prints diagnostic summaries, but the prompt smoke assertion does not make those facts a mapping-safety proof.
- The automated QEMU prompt smoke test asserts the cloned CR3 transition, the applicable active-PCID/global-TLB invalidation marker, kernel HHDM alias permissions/cache preservation, heap probe, and shell prompt. The current emulator reports CR4.PGE clear; it exercises the CR3 reload path, not the PGE-toggle global flush path. `just frame-smoke` additionally exercises one allocator-owned frame, inherited paths, kernel/HHDM cache aliases, and a separate candidate mapping through Limine's HHDM contract. The clone preserves Limine's complete reachable hierarchy, but there is no clean-room mapping policy or exhaustive audit of unrelated aliases; emulator tests do not establish physical-hardware behavior. `just fault-smoke` exercises only the controlled page-fault and invalid-opcode fatal paths; it does not test every exception vector or recovery.
- A separate manual QEMU session exercised directory navigation and file create/write/append/read/copy/move/remove operations, including `cp` replacing an existing destination and rejection of `rmdir` on a nonempty directory. This is not exhaustive shell coverage and does not prove persistence across reboot.
- There is no on-disk filesystem integration test, syscall/userspace test, fuzz target, or physical-hardware test.

## Validation policy

For changes to the kernel entry, linker script, boot requests, architecture code, shell, or VFS, run `just verify`. For memory-management and ABI code, add negative tests for overflow, malformed ranges, permission failures, and invalid user pointers before exposing those paths to userspace.

Record commands actually run and any environment limitation in change summaries; never call an unexecuted build “passing.”

//! Fixed-capacity single-vCPU kernel-thread runtime and scheduling smoke tests.
//!
//! Thread stacks are allocator-owned 4 KiB mappings with one unmapped lower
//! guard page. Scheduler state is mutated only with local interrupts disabled.
//! The PIT handler may preempt a running thread by suspending its own call stack
//! on that thread's kernel stack and switching to another saved context.

use crate::kprintln;
use core::arch::asm;
#[cfg(feature = "probe-kernel-threads")]
use core::hint::spin_loop;
use core::sync::atomic::{AtomicPtr, AtomicUsize, Ordering};
use rustix_kernel::frame::{Frame, FrameAllocator};

use rustix_kernel::paging::{
    validate_mapping_range, CachePolicy, CandidatePageTableMemory, CandidatePageTables,
    EffectiveMemoryType, MtrrState, PagePermissions, PageWalkOutcome, PatLayout, PAGE_SIZE,
};
use rustix_kernel::scheduler::{
    initialize_thread_context_stack, Scheduler, SchedulerError, ThreadId, ThreadState, WaitQueueId,
};
use rustix_kernel::time::AtomicTickCounter;

const MAX_THREADS: usize = 2;
const THREAD_STACK_PAGES: usize = 4;
const THREAD_STACK_STRIDE: u64 = (THREAD_STACK_PAGES as u64 + 1) * PAGE_SIZE;
const THREAD_STACK_VIRTUAL_BASE: u64 = 0xffff_c400_0000_0000;
const CONTEXT_COUNT: usize = MAX_THREADS + 1;
const QUEUE_COUNT: usize = MAX_THREADS + 1;
const _: [(); QUEUE_COUNT] = [(); MAX_THREADS + 1];

#[repr(C, align(16))]
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct FxSaveArea([u8; 512]);

impl FxSaveArea {
    const INITIAL: Self = {
        let mut bytes = [0; 512];
        bytes[0] = 0x7f;
        bytes[1] = 0x03;
        bytes[24] = 0x80;
        bytes[25] = 0x1f;
        Self(bytes)
    };
}

const _: [(); 512] = [(); core::mem::size_of::<FxSaveArea>()];
const _: [(); 16] = [(); core::mem::align_of::<FxSaveArea>()];

static THREAD_TEST_TRACE: AtomicUsize = AtomicUsize::new(0);
static ACTIVE_RUNTIME: AtomicPtr<KernelThreadRuntime> = AtomicPtr::new(core::ptr::null_mut());
static mut BOOTSTRAP_FX_STATE: FxSaveArea = FxSaveArea::INITIAL;
#[export_name = "rustix_active_fpu_state_pointer"]
static mut ACTIVE_FX_STATE_POINTER: *mut FxSaveArea = core::ptr::null_mut();

/// Initialize the IRQ assembly's FXSAVE destination before any IRQ route is armed.
pub(crate) fn initialize_fpu_context() {
    // SAFETY: Bootstrap runs with IF clear and this pointer is published before
    // the timer or device IRQ routes can be unmasked.
    unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(ACTIVE_FX_STATE_POINTER)
            .write(core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(BOOTSTRAP_FX_STATE));
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-kernel-threads")]
static PREEMPTION_A_STARTED: AtomicUsize = AtomicUsize::new(0);
#[cfg(feature = "probe-kernel-threads")]
static PREEMPTION_B_STARTED: AtomicUsize = AtomicUsize::new(0);
#[cfg(feature = "probe-kernel-threads")]
static PREEMPTION_TEST_FAILED: AtomicUsize = AtomicUsize::new(0);
#[cfg(feature = "probe-kernel-threads")]
static PREEMPTION_FPU_FAILED: AtomicUsize = AtomicUsize::new(0);
#[cfg(feature = "probe-kernel-threads")]
const PREEMPTION_TEST_TICK_BUDGET: u64 = 8;
#[cfg(feature = "probe-kernel-threads")]
const PREEMPTION_PATTERN_A: [u8; 16] = [0xa1; 16];
#[cfg(feature = "probe-kernel-threads")]
const PREEMPTION_PATTERN_B: [u8; 16] = [0xb2; 16];

type ThreadEntry = extern "C" fn(*mut (), usize);

struct KernelThreadRuntime {
    policy: Scheduler<MAX_THREADS, QUEUE_COUNT, MAX_THREADS>,
    saved_rsp: [usize; CONTEXT_COUNT],
    fx_state: [FxSaveArea; CONTEXT_COUNT],
    thread_ids: [Option<ThreadId>; MAX_THREADS],
    stack_virtual_starts: [Option<u64>; MAX_THREADS],
    entries: [Option<ThreadEntry>; MAX_THREADS],
    arguments: [usize; MAX_THREADS],
    deadlines: [Option<u64>; MAX_THREADS],
    event_queue: WaitQueueId,
    timer_queues: [WaitQueueId; MAX_THREADS],
    current_context: usize,
    input_events_enabled: bool,
    ticks: &'static AtomicTickCounter,
}

impl KernelThreadRuntime {
    fn new(ticks: &'static AtomicTickCounter) -> Result<Self, SchedulerError> {
        let mut policy = Scheduler::new();
        let event_queue = policy.create_wait_queue()?;
        let mut timer_queues = [event_queue; MAX_THREADS];
        for queue in &mut timer_queues {
            *queue = policy.create_wait_queue()?;
        }
        Ok(Self {
            policy,
            saved_rsp: [0; CONTEXT_COUNT],
            fx_state: [FxSaveArea::INITIAL; CONTEXT_COUNT],
            thread_ids: [None; MAX_THREADS],
            stack_virtual_starts: [None; MAX_THREADS],
            entries: [None; MAX_THREADS],
            arguments: [0; MAX_THREADS],
            deadlines: [None; MAX_THREADS],
            event_queue,
            timer_queues,
            current_context: 0,
            input_events_enabled: false,
            ticks,
        })
    }

    fn all_threads_exited(&self) -> bool {
        self.thread_ids
            .iter()
            .flatten()
            .all(|thread| self.policy.state(*thread) == Ok(ThreadState::Exited))
    }

    fn wake_expired(&mut self) {
        let now = self.ticks.ticks();
        for slot in 0..MAX_THREADS {
            if self.deadlines[slot].is_some_and(|deadline| now >= deadline) {
                self.deadlines[slot] = None;
                if self.policy.wake_one(self.timer_queues[slot]).is_err() {
                    THREAD_TEST_TRACE.store(99, Ordering::Release);
                }
            }
        }
    }

    fn wake_ready_events(&mut self) -> bool {
        self.wake_expired();
        let input_event = self.input_events_enabled
            && rustix_kernel::input::INPUT_EVENT_PENDING.swap(false, Ordering::AcqRel);
        if input_event && self.policy.wake_all(self.event_queue).is_err() {
            THREAD_TEST_TRACE.store(99, Ordering::Release);
        }
        input_event
    }

    unsafe fn run_from_raw(runtime_pointer: *mut Self) {
        let initial_flags = disable_interrupts();
        if ACTIVE_RUNTIME
            .compare_exchange(
                core::ptr::null_mut(),
                runtime_pointer,
                Ordering::Release,
                Ordering::Relaxed,
            )
            .is_err()
        {
            halt_on_stack_cleanup_failure();
        }
        let first = {
            // SAFETY: The caller supplies the live, exclusively owned runtime;
            // the temporary reference ends before the context switch.
            let runtime = unsafe { &mut *runtime_pointer };
            match runtime.policy.dispatch() {
                Ok(Some(thread)) => {
                    let context = thread.slot_index() + 1;
                    runtime.current_context = context;
                    Some((context, runtime.saved_rsp[context]))
                }
                Ok(None) => None,
                Err(_) => {
                    THREAD_TEST_TRACE.store(99, Ordering::Release);
                    None
                }
            }
        };
        if let Some((new_context, new_rsp)) = first {
            // SAFETY: Context zero is the active bootstrap stack; the selected
            // synthetic frame and both aligned FXSAVE areas remain live.
            unsafe {
                rustix_arch_context_switch(
                    core::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*runtime_pointer).saved_rsp[0]),
                    new_rsp as *mut usize,
                    core::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*runtime_pointer).fx_state[0]),
                    core::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*runtime_pointer).fx_state[new_context]),
                );
            }
        }
        restore_interrupts(initial_flags);

        loop {
            let flags = disable_interrupts();
            let (new_context, new_rsp, finished) = {
                // SAFETY: No other thread runs while IF is clear. All mutable
                // scheduler borrows end before any subsequent context switch.
                let runtime = unsafe { &mut *runtime_pointer };
                runtime.wake_ready_events();
                if runtime.all_threads_exited() {
                    (None, None, true)
                } else {
                    match runtime.policy.dispatch() {
                        Ok(Some(thread)) => {
                            let context = thread.slot_index() + 1;
                            runtime.current_context = context;
                            (Some(context), Some(runtime.saved_rsp[context]), false)
                        }
                        Ok(None) => (None, None, false),
                        Err(_) => {
                            THREAD_TEST_TRACE.store(99, Ordering::Release);
                            (None, None, true)
                        }
                    }
                }
            };
            if finished {
                ACTIVE_RUNTIME.store(core::ptr::null_mut(), Ordering::Release);
                unsafe { save_bootstrap_fx_state() };
                restore_interrupts(flags);
                return;
            }
            if let (Some(new_context), Some(new_rsp)) = (new_context, new_rsp) {
                // SAFETY: The bootstrap context is currently active and the
                // selected stack and FXSAVE area remain owned by this runtime.
                unsafe {
                    rustix_arch_context_switch(
                        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*runtime_pointer).saved_rsp[0]),
                        new_rsp as *mut usize,
                        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*runtime_pointer).fx_state[0]),
                        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*runtime_pointer).fx_state[new_context]),
                    );
                }
                restore_interrupts(flags);
            } else {
                // `sti; hlt` is atomic with respect to the interrupt shadow, so
                // a PIT wakeup cannot be lost between checking deadlines and halt.
                // SAFETY: The verified PIT handler is installed and the only
                // unmasked device route; it performs no allocation or scheduling.
                unsafe { asm!("sti; hlt") };
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Run a single long-lived cooperative worker on an owned guarded stack.
pub fn run_shell<M: CandidatePageTableMemory>(
    candidate: &mut CandidatePageTables<'_, M>,
    allocator: *mut FrameAllocator,
    cpu_info: &crate::arch::x86_64::cpu::CpuInfo,
    ticks: &'static AtomicTickCounter,
    entry: extern "C" fn(*mut (), usize),
    argument: usize,
) -> ! {
    let mut runtime =
        KernelThreadRuntime::new(ticks).unwrap_or_else(|_| halt_on_stack_cleanup_failure());
    runtime.input_events_enabled = true;
    let runtime_pointer = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(runtime);
    let flags = disable_interrupts();
    // SAFETY: The caller supplies the live allocator retained by BootInfo. This
    // exclusive borrow is limited to stack setup and ends before context switches.
    let spawned = unsafe {
        spawn_thread(
            &mut runtime,
            candidate,
            &mut *allocator,
            cpu_info,
            runtime_pointer,
            entry,
            argument,
        )
    };
    if spawned.is_err() {
        restore_interrupts(flags);
        halt_on_stack_cleanup_failure();
    }
    restore_interrupts(flags);
    // SAFETY: The caller keeps the active root, allocator, CPU snapshot, thread
    // context, and callback argument alive for this non-returning kernel runtime.
    unsafe { KernelThreadRuntime::run_from_raw(runtime_pointer) };
    let flags = disable_interrupts();
    // SAFETY: No worker is running after `run_from_raw` returns, so the raw
    // allocator pointer is exclusively available for final stack cleanup.
    let allocator = unsafe { &mut *allocator };
    reap_exited_stacks(&mut runtime, candidate, allocator);
    restore_interrupts(flags);
    halt_on_stack_cleanup_failure()
}

/// Block the current cooperative thread until an input IRQ publishes an event.
pub(crate) fn wait_for_input(runtime_pointer: *mut ()) {
    // SAFETY: Only a normal cooperative thread calls this; IRQ handlers merely
    // publish the atomic event and never touch scheduler policy state.
    if !unsafe { block_current(runtime_pointer.cast(), None) } {
        THREAD_TEST_TRACE.store(99, Ordering::Release);
    }
}

/// Exercise real switching, stack guards, event wakeup, timed sleep, and timer preemption.
/// The caller must provide the current active root, keep this single-vCPU kernel
/// path alive for the call, and have already enabled the verified PIT route.
#[cfg(feature = "probe-kernel-threads")]
pub fn smoke<M: CandidatePageTableMemory>(
    candidate: &mut CandidatePageTables<'_, M>,
    allocator: &mut FrameAllocator,
    cpu_info: &crate::arch::x86_64::cpu::CpuInfo,
    ticks: &'static AtomicTickCounter,
) -> Result<(), &'static str> {
    THREAD_TEST_TRACE.store(0, Ordering::Release);
    if !irq_spin_lock_preserves_interrupt_state() {
        return Err("IRQ-save spin lock failed to mask or restore IF");
    }
    kprintln!("IRQ-save lock path passed: prior IF state preserved");

    let mut runtime = KernelThreadRuntime::new(ticks).map_err(|_| "scheduler setup failed")?;
    let runtime_pointer = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(runtime);

    let flags = disable_interrupts();
    let first = spawn_thread(
        &mut runtime,
        candidate,
        allocator,
        cpu_info,
        runtime_pointer,
        waiter_thread,
        0,
    );
    let second = if first.is_ok() {
        spawn_thread(
            &mut runtime,
            candidate,
            allocator,
            cpu_info,
            runtime_pointer,
            signaler_thread,
            0,
        )
    } else {
        Err("waiter thread stack setup failed")
    };
    restore_interrupts(flags);

    if first.is_err() || second.is_err() {
        cancel_unstarted_threads(&mut runtime);
        let flags = disable_interrupts();
        reap_exited_stacks(&mut runtime, candidate, allocator);
        restore_interrupts(flags);
        return Err(first
            .err()
            .or(second.err())
            .unwrap_or("thread setup failed"));
    }

    // Every stack slot was checked page by page during setup: the lower guard is
    // absent, and all four stack leaves are supervisor RW/NX with the selected WB type.
    kprintln!("kernel thread stacks verified: mapped RW/NX with absent lower guards");
    // SAFETY: The runtime remains on the bootstrap stack and is passed by raw
    // pointer; no mutable reference is retained across the context switches.
    unsafe { KernelThreadRuntime::run_from_raw(runtime_pointer) };

    let passed = THREAD_TEST_TRACE.load(Ordering::Acquire) == 5
        && ticks.ticks() >= 2
        && runtime.all_threads_exited();
    let flags = disable_interrupts();
    reap_exited_stacks(&mut runtime, candidate, allocator);
    restore_interrupts(flags);
    if !passed {
        return Err("cooperative yield/wakeup/timed-sleep sequence failed");
    }
    kprintln!("cooperative thread path passed: yield, event wakeup, timed sleep, stack guards");
    timer_preemption_smoke(candidate, allocator, cpu_info, ticks)
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-kernel-threads")]
fn irq_spin_lock_preserves_interrupt_state() -> bool {
    use rustix_kernel::sync::IrqSpinLock;

    fn interrupts_enabled() -> bool {
        let flags: u64;
        // SAFETY: Reading RFLAGS is non-mutating in the CPL 0 QEMU probe.
        unsafe { asm!("pushfq", "pop {}", out(reg) flags) };
        flags & (1 << 9) != 0
    }

    let lock = IrqSpinLock::new(());
    let initially_enabled = interrupts_enabled();
    let masked_while_held = {
        let _guard = lock.lock();
        !interrupts_enabled()
    };
    let restored_after_enabled = interrupts_enabled() == initially_enabled;

    let flags = disable_interrupts();
    let masked_while_already_disabled = {
        let _guard = lock.lock();
        !interrupts_enabled()
    };
    let remained_disabled_after_drop = !interrupts_enabled();
    restore_interrupts(flags);

    initially_enabled
        && masked_while_held
        && restored_after_enabled
        && masked_while_already_disabled
        && remained_disabled_after_drop
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-kernel-threads")]
fn timer_preemption_smoke<M: CandidatePageTableMemory>(
    candidate: &mut CandidatePageTables<'_, M>,
    allocator: &mut FrameAllocator,
    cpu_info: &crate::arch::x86_64::cpu::CpuInfo,
    ticks: &'static AtomicTickCounter,
) -> Result<(), &'static str> {
    PREEMPTION_A_STARTED.store(0, Ordering::Release);
    PREEMPTION_B_STARTED.store(0, Ordering::Release);
    PREEMPTION_TEST_FAILED.store(0, Ordering::Release);
    PREEMPTION_FPU_FAILED.store(0, Ordering::Release);

    let mut runtime =
        KernelThreadRuntime::new(ticks).map_err(|_| "preemption scheduler setup failed")?;
    let runtime_pointer = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(runtime);
    let ticks_pointer = ticks as *const AtomicTickCounter as usize;

    let flags = disable_interrupts();
    let first = spawn_thread(
        &mut runtime,
        candidate,
        allocator,
        cpu_info,
        runtime_pointer,
        non_yielding_preemption_worker_a,
        ticks_pointer,
    );
    let second = if first.is_ok() {
        spawn_thread(
            &mut runtime,
            candidate,
            allocator,
            cpu_info,
            runtime_pointer,
            non_yielding_preemption_worker_b,
            ticks_pointer,
        )
    } else {
        Err("first preemption worker stack setup failed")
    };
    restore_interrupts(flags);

    if first.is_err() || second.is_err() {
        cancel_unstarted_threads(&mut runtime);
        let flags = disable_interrupts();
        reap_exited_stacks(&mut runtime, candidate, allocator);
        restore_interrupts(flags);
        return Err(first
            .err()
            .or(second.err())
            .unwrap_or("preemption worker setup failed"));
    }

    // Both workers busy-wait without yielding. Worker B can start only after a
    // PIT interrupt preempts worker A. Worker A also checks that its live XMM0
    // value survives the interrupt handler and another thread's execution.
    unsafe { KernelThreadRuntime::run_from_raw(runtime_pointer) };
    let passed = PREEMPTION_A_STARTED.load(Ordering::Acquire) == 1
        && PREEMPTION_B_STARTED.load(Ordering::Acquire) == 1
        && PREEMPTION_TEST_FAILED.load(Ordering::Acquire) == 0
        && PREEMPTION_FPU_FAILED.load(Ordering::Acquire) == 0
        && runtime.all_threads_exited();
    let flags = disable_interrupts();
    reap_exited_stacks(&mut runtime, candidate, allocator);
    restore_interrupts(flags);
    if !passed {
        return Err("timer did not preempt a non-yielding thread within the tick budget");
    }
    kprintln!("timer preemption path passed: non-yielding workers and FPU state survived");
    Ok(())
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-kernel-threads")]
extern "C" fn non_yielding_preemption_worker_a(_runtime: *mut (), ticks_pointer: usize) {
    PREEMPTION_A_STARTED.store(1, Ordering::Release);
    let ticks = unsafe { &*(ticks_pointer as *const AtomicTickCounter) };
    let deadline = ticks.ticks().saturating_add(PREEMPTION_TEST_TICK_BUDGET);
    unsafe {
        asm!(
            "movdqu xmm0, xmmword ptr [{pattern}]",
            pattern = in(reg) PREEMPTION_PATTERN_A.as_ptr(),
            out("xmm0") _,
            options(readonly, nostack, preserves_flags),
        );
    }
    while PREEMPTION_B_STARTED.load(Ordering::Acquire) == 0 {
        if ticks.ticks() >= deadline {
            PREEMPTION_TEST_FAILED.store(1, Ordering::Release);
            break;
        }
        spin_loop();
    }
    let mut saved_state = core::mem::MaybeUninit::<FxSaveArea>::uninit();
    // SAFETY: `FxSaveArea` is 16-byte aligned and exactly 512 bytes; FXSAVE
    // writes the complete legacy x87/SSE state image before it is inspected.
    unsafe {
        asm!(
            "fxsave64 [{state}]",
            state = in(reg) saved_state.as_mut_ptr(),
            options(nostack),
        );
    }
    // SAFETY: The preceding FXSAVE initialized every byte of the state image.
    let saved_state = unsafe { saved_state.assume_init() };
    if saved_state.0[160..176] != PREEMPTION_PATTERN_A {
        PREEMPTION_FPU_FAILED.store(1, Ordering::Release);
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-kernel-threads")]
extern "C" fn non_yielding_preemption_worker_b(_runtime: *mut (), _ticks_pointer: usize) {
    unsafe {
        asm!(
            "movdqu xmm0, xmmword ptr [{pattern}]",
            pattern = in(reg) PREEMPTION_PATTERN_B.as_ptr(),
            out("xmm0") _,
            options(readonly, nostack, preserves_flags),
        );
    }
    PREEMPTION_B_STARTED.store(1, Ordering::Release);
}

fn spawn_thread<M: CandidatePageTableMemory>(
    runtime: &mut KernelThreadRuntime,
    candidate: &mut CandidatePageTables<'_, M>,
    allocator: &mut FrameAllocator,
    cpu_info: &crate::arch::x86_64::cpu::CpuInfo,
    runtime_pointer: *mut KernelThreadRuntime,
    entry: ThreadEntry,
    argument: usize,
) -> Result<ThreadId, &'static str> {
    let slot = runtime
        .thread_ids
        .iter()
        .position(Option::is_none)
        .ok_or("thread capacity exhausted")?;
    let region_start = THREAD_STACK_VIRTUAL_BASE
        .checked_add(
            (slot as u64)
                .checked_mul(THREAD_STACK_STRIDE)
                .ok_or("stack VA overflow")?,
        )
        .ok_or("stack VA overflow")?;
    let stack_start = region_start
        .checked_add(PAGE_SIZE)
        .ok_or("stack VA overflow")?;

    for page in 0..=THREAD_STACK_PAGES {
        let address = region_start + page as u64 * PAGE_SIZE;
        if !matches!(
            candidate.walk(address),
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::NotPresent { .. })
        ) {
            return Err("thread guard or stack VA is already mapped");
        }
    }

    let physical_width = cpu_info
        .physical_address_bits
        .ok_or("physical width unavailable")?;
    let pat = PatLayout::from_msr_value(cpu_info.pat_msr_value.ok_or("PAT unavailable")?)
        .map_err(|_| "PAT state invalid")?;
    let mtrrs = match &cpu_info.mtrr {
        MtrrState::Captured(registers) => registers
            .validated_layout(physical_width)
            .map_err(|_| "MTRR state invalid")?,
        _ => return Err("MTRR state unavailable"),
    };
    let permissions = PagePermissions {
        writable: true,
        executable: false,
        user_accessible: false,
    };
    let mut mapped_pages = 0usize;
    for page in 0..THREAD_STACK_PAGES {
        let virtual_address = stack_start + page as u64 * PAGE_SIZE;
        let frame = allocator.allocate().ok_or_else(|| {
            rollback_stack(candidate, allocator, stack_start, mapped_pages);
            "physical frames exhausted for thread stack"
        })?;
        let mapping = match validate_mapping_range(
            virtual_address,
            frame.address(),
            PAGE_SIZE,
            permissions,
            Some(physical_width),
            cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        ) {
            Ok(mapping) => mapping,
            Err(_) => {
                deallocate_or_halt(allocator, frame);
                rollback_stack(candidate, allocator, stack_start, mapped_pages);
                return Err("thread stack mapping rejected");
            }
        };
        let attributes = match mapping.select_cache_attributes(
            CachePolicy::WriteBack,
            pat,
            &mtrrs,
            cpu_info.normal_caching,
        ) {
            Ok(attributes) if attributes.effective_type() == EffectiveMemoryType::WriteBack => {
                attributes
            }
            _ => {
                deallocate_or_halt(allocator, frame);
                rollback_stack(candidate, allocator, stack_start, mapped_pages);
                return Err("thread stack has no uniform write-back policy");
            }
        };
        // SAFETY: The active root is current on this single CPU; IF is clear
        // throughout stack setup, and each mapping uses an allocator-owned frame.
        if let Err(failure) =
            unsafe { candidate.map_owned_page_active(allocator, frame, mapping, attributes) }
        {
            deallocate_or_halt(allocator, failure.frame);
            rollback_stack(candidate, allocator, stack_start, mapped_pages);
            return Err("thread stack mapping failed");
        }
        match candidate.walk(virtual_address) {
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation))
                if translation.permissions == permissions
                    && translation.pat_index == attributes.pat_index() => {}
            _ => {
                rollback_stack(candidate, allocator, stack_start, mapped_pages + 1);
                return Err("thread stack page-table verification failed");
            }
        }
        mapped_pages += 1;
    }

    let stack_top = stack_start + THREAD_STACK_PAGES as u64 * PAGE_SIZE;
    let frame_word_count = 16;
    let frame_words = unsafe {
        core::slice::from_raw_parts_mut(
            (stack_top as *mut usize).sub(frame_word_count),
            frame_word_count,
        )
    };
    let registers = [0, slot, runtime_pointer as usize, 0, 0, 0];
    let saved_rsp = initialize_thread_context_stack(
        frame_words,
        registers,
        kernel_thread_trampoline as *const () as usize,
    );
    let Some(saved_rsp) = saved_rsp else {
        rollback_stack(candidate, allocator, stack_start, mapped_pages);
        return Err("thread initial context frame did not fit");
    };
    let thread = match runtime.policy.create_thread() {
        Ok(thread) if thread.slot_index() == slot => thread,
        Ok(_) => {
            rollback_stack(candidate, allocator, stack_start, mapped_pages);
            return Err("scheduler slot and stack slot diverged");
        }
        Err(_) => {
            rollback_stack(candidate, allocator, stack_start, mapped_pages);
            return Err("scheduler thread capacity exhausted");
        }
    };
    runtime.thread_ids[slot] = Some(thread);
    runtime.stack_virtual_starts[slot] = Some(stack_start);
    runtime.entries[slot] = Some(entry);
    runtime.arguments[slot] = argument;
    runtime.saved_rsp[slot + 1] = saved_rsp;
    Ok(thread)
}

fn rollback_stack<M: CandidatePageTableMemory>(
    candidate: &mut CandidatePageTables<'_, M>,
    allocator: &mut FrameAllocator,
    stack_start: u64,
    mapped_pages: usize,
) {
    for page in (0..mapped_pages).rev() {
        let virtual_address = stack_start + page as u64 * PAGE_SIZE;
        // SAFETY: Stack setup keeps IF clear and this candidate is the active
        // root; the frame is not returned until `invlpg` completes.
        let frame = unsafe { candidate.unmap_owned_page_active(virtual_address) }
            .unwrap_or_else(|_| halt_on_stack_cleanup_failure());
        deallocate_or_halt(allocator, frame);
    }
}

fn reap_exited_stacks<M: CandidatePageTableMemory>(
    runtime: &mut KernelThreadRuntime,
    candidate: &mut CandidatePageTables<'_, M>,
    allocator: &mut FrameAllocator,
) {
    for slot in 0..MAX_THREADS {
        let Some(thread) = runtime.thread_ids[slot] else {
            continue;
        };
        if runtime.policy.state(thread) != Ok(ThreadState::Exited) {
            continue;
        }
        let stack_start =
            runtime.stack_virtual_starts[slot].unwrap_or_else(|| halt_on_stack_cleanup_failure());
        rollback_stack(candidate, allocator, stack_start, THREAD_STACK_PAGES);
        runtime
            .policy
            .reap(thread)
            .unwrap_or_else(|_| halt_on_stack_cleanup_failure());
        runtime.thread_ids[slot] = None;
        runtime.stack_virtual_starts[slot] = None;
        runtime.entries[slot] = None;
        runtime.arguments[slot] = 0;
        runtime.deadlines[slot] = None;
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-kernel-threads")]
fn cancel_unstarted_threads(runtime: &mut KernelThreadRuntime) {
    loop {
        match runtime.policy.dispatch() {
            Ok(Some(_)) => {
                if runtime.policy.exit_current().is_err() {
                    halt_on_stack_cleanup_failure();
                }
            }
            Ok(None) => return,
            Err(_) => halt_on_stack_cleanup_failure(),
        }
    }
}

fn deallocate_or_halt(allocator: &mut FrameAllocator, frame: Frame) {
    if let Err(failure) = allocator.deallocate(frame) {
        kprintln!("thread stack frame release failed: {:?}", failure.error);
        halt_on_stack_cleanup_failure();
    }
}

fn halt_on_stack_cleanup_failure() -> ! {
    loop {
        // SAFETY: Losing stack-frame ownership is fatal; stop without touching
        // any potentially inconsistent scheduler or allocator state.
        unsafe { asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    }
}

extern "C" fn kernel_thread_trampoline() -> ! {
    let runtime_pointer: *mut KernelThreadRuntime;
    let slot: usize;
    // SAFETY: The initial stack frame restores the runtime pointer in R13 and
    // the generation-checked policy slot index in R14 before this entry.
    unsafe {
        asm!("mov {}, r13", out(reg) runtime_pointer, options(nomem, nostack, preserves_flags));
        asm!("mov {}, r14", out(reg) slot, options(nomem, nostack, preserves_flags));
    }
    let (entry, argument) = {
        // SAFETY: The runtime is live on the retained bootstrap stack and the
        // selected slot was initialized before its context became dispatchable.
        let runtime = unsafe { &*runtime_pointer };
        let entry = runtime.entries[slot].unwrap_or_else(|| halt_on_stack_cleanup_failure());
        (entry, runtime.arguments[slot])
    };
    // New cooperative contexts start with IF clear. Enable the already-verified
    // timer route only after their descriptor and runtime state are available.
    // SAFETY: The scheduler installs no thread until the caller has configured
    // the timer and registered its bounded non-scheduling handler.
    unsafe { asm!("sti") };
    entry(runtime_pointer.cast(), argument);
    // SAFETY: This thread's entry returned normally; mark it exited and switch
    // away before its stack can be reclaimed by the bootstrap context.
    unsafe { exit_current(runtime_pointer) }
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-kernel-threads")]
extern "C" fn waiter_thread(runtime: *mut (), _argument: usize) {
    THREAD_TEST_TRACE.store(1, Ordering::Release);
    if !wait_for_event(runtime) || THREAD_TEST_TRACE.load(Ordering::Acquire) != 2 {
        THREAD_TEST_TRACE.store(99, Ordering::Release);
        return;
    }
    THREAD_TEST_TRACE.store(3, Ordering::Release);
    if !sleep_for_ticks(runtime, 2) || THREAD_TEST_TRACE.load(Ordering::Acquire) != 4 {
        THREAD_TEST_TRACE.store(99, Ordering::Release);
        return;
    }
    THREAD_TEST_TRACE.store(5, Ordering::Release);
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-kernel-threads")]
extern "C" fn signaler_thread(runtime: *mut (), _argument: usize) {
    if THREAD_TEST_TRACE.load(Ordering::Acquire) != 1 {
        THREAD_TEST_TRACE.store(99, Ordering::Release);
        return;
    }
    THREAD_TEST_TRACE.store(2, Ordering::Release);
    if !wake_event(runtime) {
        THREAD_TEST_TRACE.store(99, Ordering::Release);
        return;
    }
    yield_current(runtime);
    if THREAD_TEST_TRACE.load(Ordering::Acquire) != 3 {
        THREAD_TEST_TRACE.store(99, Ordering::Release);
        return;
    }
    THREAD_TEST_TRACE.store(4, Ordering::Release);
    while THREAD_TEST_TRACE.load(Ordering::Acquire) != 5 {
        yield_current(runtime);
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-kernel-threads")]
fn wait_for_event(runtime_pointer: *mut ()) -> bool {
    // SAFETY: This is an ordinary cooperative thread, never an IRQ handler.
    unsafe { block_current(runtime_pointer.cast(), None) }
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-kernel-threads")]
fn sleep_for_ticks(runtime_pointer: *mut (), delay: u64) -> bool {
    if delay == 0 {
        return true;
    }
    // SAFETY: The runtime pointer is restored from this thread's initial context;
    // the runtime remains alive until every thread has exited and been reaped.
    unsafe { block_current(runtime_pointer.cast(), Some(delay)) }
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-kernel-threads")]
fn wake_event(runtime_pointer: *mut ()) -> bool {
    let flags = disable_interrupts();
    // SAFETY: IF is clear and only the current cooperative thread mutates policy.
    let result = unsafe {
        let runtime = &mut *runtime_pointer.cast::<KernelThreadRuntime>();
        runtime.policy.wake_one(runtime.event_queue).is_ok()
    };
    restore_interrupts(flags);
    result
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-kernel-threads")]
fn yield_current(runtime_pointer: *mut ()) {
    let flags = disable_interrupts();
    let switch = unsafe {
        let runtime = &mut *runtime_pointer.cast::<KernelThreadRuntime>();
        runtime.wake_ready_events();
        let Some(current) = runtime.policy.current() else {
            restore_interrupts(flags);
            return;
        };
        let old_context = runtime.current_context;
        let next = match runtime.policy.yield_current() {
            Ok(next) => next,
            Err(_) => {
                THREAD_TEST_TRACE.store(99, Ordering::Release);
                restore_interrupts(flags);
                return;
            }
        };
        let next_context = next.slot_index() + 1;
        runtime.current_context = next_context;
        if current == next {
            None
        } else {
            Some((
                core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(runtime.saved_rsp[old_context]),
                runtime.saved_rsp[next_context],
                core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(runtime.fx_state[old_context]),
                core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(runtime.fx_state[next_context]),
            ))
        }
    };
    if let Some((old_rsp, new_rsp, old_fx_state, new_fx_state)) = switch {
        // SAFETY: The selected contexts are same-CPU kernel stacks, and the
        // temporary scheduler borrows end before switching their saved FPU state.
        unsafe {
            rustix_arch_context_switch(old_rsp, new_rsp as *mut usize, old_fx_state, new_fx_state)
        };
    }
    restore_interrupts(flags);
}

unsafe fn block_current(runtime_pointer: *mut KernelThreadRuntime, delay: Option<u64>) -> bool {
    let flags = disable_interrupts();
    let switch = {
        // SAFETY: Called from one cooperative thread with IF clear; the state
        // references are scoped entirely before the context switch.
        let runtime = unsafe { &mut *runtime_pointer };
        let input_event = runtime.wake_ready_events();
        if delay.is_none() && runtime.input_events_enabled && input_event {
            restore_interrupts(flags);
            return true;
        }
        let Some(current) = runtime.policy.current() else {
            restore_interrupts(flags);
            return false;
        };
        let slot = current.slot_index();
        let queue = if let Some(delay) = delay {
            let deadline = runtime.ticks.ticks().saturating_add(delay);
            runtime.deadlines[slot] = Some(deadline);
            runtime.timer_queues[slot]
        } else {
            runtime.event_queue
        };
        let next = match runtime.policy.sleep_current(queue) {
            Ok(next) => next,
            Err(_) => {
                runtime.deadlines[slot] = None;
                restore_interrupts(flags);
                return false;
            }
        };
        let next_context = next.map_or(0, |thread| thread.slot_index() + 1);
        let old_context = runtime.current_context;
        runtime.current_context = next_context;
        Some((
            core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(runtime.saved_rsp[old_context]),
            runtime.saved_rsp[next_context],
            core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(runtime.fx_state[old_context]),
            core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(runtime.fx_state[next_context]),
        ))
    };
    if let Some((old_rsp, new_rsp, old_fx_state, new_fx_state)) = switch {
        // SAFETY: The current thread is blocked and cannot run until a later
        // wake; both stack and FXSAVE areas remain live in the runtime.
        unsafe {
            rustix_arch_context_switch(old_rsp, new_rsp as *mut usize, old_fx_state, new_fx_state)
        };
    }
    restore_interrupts(flags);
    true
}

unsafe fn exit_current(runtime_pointer: *mut KernelThreadRuntime) -> ! {
    let flags = disable_interrupts();
    let (old_rsp, new_rsp, old_fx_state, new_fx_state) = {
        // SAFETY: This is the current thread's normal return path, with IF clear.
        let runtime = unsafe { &mut *runtime_pointer };
        runtime.wake_ready_events();
        let old_context = runtime.current_context;
        match runtime.policy.exit_current() {
            Ok(next) => {
                let next_context = next.map_or(0, |thread| thread.slot_index() + 1);
                runtime.current_context = next_context;
                (
                    core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(runtime.saved_rsp[old_context]),
                    runtime.saved_rsp[next_context],
                    core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(runtime.fx_state[old_context]),
                    core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(runtime.fx_state[next_context]),
                )
            }
            Err(_) => halt_on_stack_cleanup_failure(),
        }
    };
    // SAFETY: The exited context is never dispatched again; the target is a
    // different ready thread or the retained bootstrap stack.
    unsafe {
        rustix_arch_context_switch(old_rsp, new_rsp as *mut usize, old_fx_state, new_fx_state)
    };
    restore_interrupts(flags);
    halt_on_stack_cleanup_failure()
}

fn disable_interrupts() -> u64 {
    let flags: u64;
    // SAFETY: Bootstrap and cooperative threads execute at CPL 0; RFLAGS is
    // saved before CLI and the stack operation is balanced.
    unsafe { asm!("pushfq", "pop {}", "cli", out(reg) flags) };
    flags
}

fn restore_interrupts(flags: u64) {
    if flags & (1 << 9) != 0 {
        // SAFETY: The caller only restores the prior IF state after its critical
        // section and after the selected stack/context is fully established.
        unsafe { asm!("sti") };
    }
}

unsafe fn rustix_arch_context_switch(
    old_rsp: *mut usize,
    new_rsp: *mut usize,
    old_fx_state: *mut FxSaveArea,
    new_fx_state: *mut FxSaveArea,
) {
    // SAFETY: The runtime maintains valid saved stack frames and aligned state
    // areas. Callers hold IF clear; publish the new area before it can receive IRQs.
    unsafe { publish_fx_state(new_fx_state) };
    // SAFETY: The context switch saves the current x87/SSE state and restores the
    // target context's initialized/saved FXSAVE image.
    unsafe {
        crate::arch::x86_64::context::context_switch(
            old_rsp,
            new_rsp,
            old_fx_state.cast(),
            new_fx_state.cast(),
        )
    };
}

unsafe fn rustix_arch_context_switch_from_irq(
    old_rsp: *mut usize,
    new_rsp: *mut usize,
    new_fx_state: *mut FxSaveArea,
) {
    // SAFETY: The IRQ stub already saved the interrupted task's FPU state before
    // entering Rust. Update the return-path target before switching away.
    unsafe { publish_fx_state(new_fx_state) };
    // SAFETY: This is called only from the configured timer IRQ handler with IF
    // clear; the target area's state is initialized and 16-byte aligned.
    unsafe {
        crate::arch::x86_64::context::context_switch_from_irq(old_rsp, new_rsp, new_fx_state.cast())
    };
}

unsafe fn publish_fx_state(state: *mut FxSaveArea) {
    // SAFETY: The single-vCPU runtime calls this only with IF clear; IRQ assembly
    // reads the pointer only while executing on that same CPU.
    unsafe { core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(ACTIVE_FX_STATE_POINTER).write(state) };
}

unsafe fn save_bootstrap_fx_state() {
    let state = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(BOOTSTRAP_FX_STATE);
    // SAFETY: FXSAVE is enabled during boot, `state` is 16-byte aligned, and the
    // caller has IF clear while the last kernel thread returns to the bootstrap.
    unsafe { asm!("fxsave64 [{}]", in(reg) state, options(nostack)) };
    // SAFETY: Interrupts remain disabled until the saved bootstrap area is active.
    unsafe { publish_fx_state(state) };
}

/// Advance scheduler deadlines/events and preempt the current thread if another
/// context is ready. Called only after the timer IRQ has sent APIC EOI.
pub(crate) fn timer_interrupt() {
    let runtime_pointer = ACTIVE_RUNTIME.load(Ordering::Acquire);
    if runtime_pointer.is_null() {
        return;
    }

    // The interrupt gate has cleared IF. Every ordinary scheduler mutation also
    // disables IF before borrowing this runtime, so the single CPU cannot observe
    // a partially updated scheduler state here.
    let switch = unsafe {
        let runtime = &mut *runtime_pointer;
        runtime.wake_ready_events();
        let Some(current) = runtime.policy.current() else {
            return;
        };
        let old_context = runtime.current_context;
        if old_context != current.slot_index() + 1 {
            halt_on_stack_cleanup_failure();
        }
        let next = runtime
            .policy
            .preempt_current()
            .unwrap_or_else(|_| halt_on_stack_cleanup_failure());
        let next_context = next.slot_index() + 1;
        runtime.current_context = next_context;
        if next == current {
            None
        } else {
            Some((
                core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(runtime.saved_rsp[old_context]),
                runtime.saved_rsp[next_context],
                core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(runtime.fx_state[next_context]),
            ))
        }
    };
    if let Some((old_rsp, new_rsp, new_fx_state)) = switch {
        // SAFETY: The interrupted context's FXSAVE image was written by the IRQ
        // stub before Rust ran. This suspends the handler stack and restores the
        // selected context; the interrupted thread later resumes through IRETQ.
        unsafe {
            rustix_arch_context_switch_from_irq(old_rsp, new_rsp as *mut usize, new_fx_state)
        };
    }
}

     5	
     6	Rustix (Rust-unix) is an experimental, 64-bit, Unix-like operating system whose kernel is written in Rust. This repository builds the kernel itself; Limine is used only as the external boot protocol/loader, not as a substitute for a Rustix kernel.
     7

    12	Prerequisites: a Rust stable toolchain, `just`, Python 3, `xorriso`, QEMU (`qemu-system-x86_64`), and the target installed by `rust-toolchain.toml` (or `rustup target add x86_64-unknown-none`). The first image build downloads a pinned Limine binary release and verifies its SHA-256.
    13	
    14	For a ready-to-use environment with these tools installed, open the repository in a Dev Container using `.devcontainer/`. The container uses Ubuntu 24.04 and includes the Rust target and `rustfmt` component from `rust-toolchain.toml`.
    15	
    16	```sh
    17	just help
    18	just fmt
    19	just test
    20	just check
    21	just build
    22	just image
    23	just smoke
    24	just run       # interactive serial shell in QEMU; exit with Ctrl+C
    25	just verify
    26	```
    27	
    28	`just build` produces `target/x86_64-unknown-none/release/rustix`. `just image` creates `target/rustix.iso`, a hybrid BIOS/UEFI image; `just smoke` checks that Crabshell reaches its prompt; and `just run` starts an interactive QEMU session attached to the current terminal.
    29	
    30	Try `pwd`, `ls /`, `mkdir notes`, `write notes/hello.txt "hello from Rustix"`, `cat notes/hello.txt`, and `cd ..` in Crabshell. Commands include `help`, `clear`, `pwd`, `meminfo`, `ls`, `cd`, `mkdir`, `touch`, `write`, `append`, `cp`, `mv`, `cat`, `rm`, and `rmdir`. The RAM filesystem holds at most 31 entries plus its root, with files capped at 1024 bytes. See [`docs/architecture/crabshell.md`](docs/architecture/crabshell.md) for the shell and filesystem contract, [`docs/development/building.md`](docs/development/building.md) for build/emulator details, and [`docs/index.md`](docs/index.md) for the documentation map.
    31	
    32	## Project principles
    33	
    34	- The kernel and operating-system implementation are Rust-first and `no_std`; architecture-specific privileged operations are isolated under `src/arch/`.
    35	- The kernel is the product. A bootloader may initialize the machine and transfer control, but policy, memory management, scheduling, and Unix-like services belong to Rustix.
    36	- Keep unsafe code small, documented, and adjacent to its hardware/protocol boundary.
    37	- Build incrementally: every roadmap milestone should have build checks, tests where practical, and updated design documentation.
    38	- Unix-like behavior is an explicit compatibility goal, not a claim of POSIX compliance today.
    39	
    40	## Repository map
    41	
    42	- `src/main.rs` — freestanding kernel entry point and Crabshell handoff.
    43	- `src/shell.rs` — serial line editor and kernel command executor.
    44	- `src/vfs.rs` — fixed-capacity volatile RAM filesystem, with host-side tests.
    45	- `crates/crabshell/` — separate `no_std` command parser crate; no I/O or filesystem coupling.
    46	- `src/boot.rs` — mutable Limine response requests, validated owned boot snapshot, and diagnostics.
    47	- `src/arch/x86_64/serial.rs` — COM1 formatted output, early polling input, and bounded IRQ RX queue.
    48	- `src/arch/x86_64/cpu.rs` — baseline CPUID vendor and feature reporting.
    49	- `src/arch/x86_64/interrupts.rs` — bootstrap GDT/TSS/IDT, fatal exception diagnostics, and IRQ entry/dispatch.
    50	- `src/arch/x86_64/keyboard.rs` — bounded PS/2 IRQ scancode queue and non-blocking polling fallback.
    51	- `src/arch/x86_64/apic.rs` — validated single-vCPU xAPIC/I/O APIC routing and PIT ticks.
    52	- `src/arch/x86_64/context.rs` — cooperative x86_64 context-switch assembly.
    53	- `src/arch/x86_64/io.rs` — narrow x86 port-I/O wrappers.
    54	- `src/memory.rs` — fixed-capacity validated physical-memory-map snapshot and host tests.
    55	- `src/frame.rs` — bounded physical frame allocator initialized from `BootInfo`; paging, heap growth, and guarded thread stacks use allocator-issued frames.
    56	- `src/acpi.rs` — bounded ACPI table validation and MADT parsing helpers.
    57	- `src/heap.rs` — fixed-capacity global heap policy and host tests.

# Gemini CLI instructions for Rustix

This file provides project-specific context for Gemini CLI and Gemini-based coding agents. Read `AGENTS.md` before editing; it is the canonical shared contract for all agents. Also follow any more specific instructions attached to the user request. Do not weaken the safety, status, or validation requirements described here and in `AGENTS.md`.

## Project identity and goal

Rustix (Rust-unix) is an experimental 64-bit Unix-like operating system with its own Rust kernel. The kernel itself is built as a `no_std` binary for `x86_64-unknown-none`. Limine is an external boot protocol/loader, not the Rustix kernel. A Python standard-library script only builds and smoke-tests the boot image; it does not implement OS behavior.

The project aims toward Unix-like services incrementally. It does not currently claim POSIX conformance, security isolation, or production readiness. Unsupported operations should produce clear failures or be documented as future work, not silently approximated.

## Current state and validation boundaries

Milestones 0–3 have met their documented local exit criteria. The repository has a Limine boot path, validated boot snapshot and memory map, CPUID reporting, a bounded physical-frame allocator, cloned active page tables, a bounded global heap, bootstrap GDT/TSS/IDT exception handling, a validated single-vCPU xAPIC/I/O APIC and PIT path, cooperative waits/yields with timer preemption, Crabshell, and a volatile fixed-capacity RAM filesystem.

Crabshell's parser is a standalone allocation-free `no_std` workspace crate. Kernel-side I/O and command execution are in `src/shell.rs`. Shell input uses bounded COM1 IRQ input with polling fallback; PS/2 IRQ input remains raw scancode reporting. The shell runs in ring 0 and is not a userspace application or a POSIX shell. `meminfo` reports validated RAM and frame counts. The bounded heap and frame-backed mappings are kernel services, but allocation is not allowed in IRQ/exception context.

Do not assume uncommitted source is validated just because a previous tree passed:

- Milestone 0–3 evidence is recorded in `AGENTS.md` and `docs/roadmap/README.md`; rerun relevant checks for current changes.
- Structural boot validation cannot prove that a non-null Limine pointer is readable; this remains a loader trust boundary.
- Scheduling is single-vCPU, with cooperative waits/yields and timer preemption. Exceptions remain fatal-only. There is no SMP, userspace, syscall ABI, persistent storage, user/kernel isolation, or general-purpose device model.

Never mark a roadmap item complete merely because an API, design, or source file exists. The relevant implementation and validation evidence must both meet that item's exit criteria.

## How to work in this repository

1. Start at the repository root. Read `AGENTS.md`, the relevant architecture document, and the actual implementation and call sites before making changes.
2. Keep the task scoped. Prefer a small, coherent, testable vertical slice; avoid speculative scaffolding or broad rewrites.
3. Identify invariants, capacity limits, failure semantics, and any unsafe boundary before coding.
4. Put architecture-independent logic in the `rustix-kernel` library when appropriate so host tests can exercise it. Keep the freestanding binary and parser crate boundaries intact.
5. Add or update tests and documentation together. If code and docs disagree, inspect the implementation and resolve the mismatch in the same change.
6. Run the narrowest relevant validation, then broaden it. Record exact commands and actual results.
7. Report files changed, behavior delivered, validation observed, and remaining risks. Do not conceal failures or say a check passed if it did not run.

Do not commit, create branches, alter project history, or modify unrelated files unless the user explicitly requests it.

## Rust, dependencies, and API constraints

- Keep kernel and OS implementation code `no_std`; use `core` rather than `std` in the kernel.
- Do not add a third-party Rust dependency without a concrete need and compatibility/security review. The existing project uses in-tree abstractions.
- The global heap is bounded: a 256 KiB BSS arena plus up to 1 MiB of frame-backed growth. Allocation is forbidden in IRQ/exception context; prefer fixed-capacity interfaces for core paths.
- Fixed-capacity data structures must document their limit, exhaustion/error behavior, and mutation guarantees on failure.
- Keep `crates/crabshell` limited to parsing and command representation. It must not depend on the VFS, kernel modules, serial I/O, or hardware.
- Treat `src/lib.rs` as the host-testable architecture-independent kernel library boundary; the freestanding binary is not a host test target.

## Memory, boot, and safety constraints

- Limine writes the response pointers into request records before entering `_start`; those records must remain in writable loaded storage.
- The boot snapshot checks pointer nullness/alignment, count limits, checked arithmetic, physical range validity, and overlap. It cannot establish that loader-provided memory is mapped/readable; the Limine handoff remains a trust boundary.
- Physical regions use half-open `[start, end)` ranges. Use checked arithmetic for every endpoint and address calculation.
- Feed only `Usable` regions to the frame allocator. Never turn ACPI, loader-reclaimable, reserved, framebuffer, bad-memory, executable/module, or unknown classifications into free frames without an explicit ownership transition.
- A frame is a physical address, not a dereferenceable pointer. HHDM access is restricted to checked full-frame, allocator-token paths that rely on the documented Limine contract. Do not access arbitrary physical addresses or change page-table ownership without a reviewed mapping and lifetime proof.
- The active page-table root is an allocator-owned clone of Limine's reachable hierarchy. Any future replacement must preserve the executing kernel image, bootstrap stack, `BootInfo`, request/response memory, GDT/TSS/IDT, exception stacks, and required direct-map/console mappings.
- The current frame allocator has fixed range metadata and is not a heap, page mapper, concurrent allocator, or scheduling primitive.

## x86_64 hardware and exception rules

- Keep port I/O, privileged instructions, raw pointer operations, and assembly isolated under `src/arch/x86_64/` and document their invariants near each unsafe block.
- Exception vectors 0–31 remain fatal-only; double faults use an IST stack, and page faults report CR2 and error bits. The validated single-vCPU APIC path enables only configured, registered IRQ routes after dispatch and EOI setup.
- The PIT timer handler increments ticks, acknowledges the local APIC, and may preempt a thread after scheduler state is safely updated. Timer switches preserve x87/SSE with FXSAVE/FXRSTOR; AVX/XSAVE is disabled. Do not broaden IRQ use or add SMP without explicit ownership and synchronization rules, tests, and emulator validation.
- When modifying exception stubs, verify CPU error-code normalization, stack layout, saved-register order, SysV stack alignment before calling Rust, GDT selectors, TSS descriptor/IST setup, and non-returning failure behavior.
- CPUID capability bits indicate support, not necessarily that a feature is enabled in CR registers or active paging.
- Hardware/boot code changes require more than host unit tests: include target check/build and emulator validation when possible. If unavailable, describe the exact blocker and keep status unverified.

## Crabshell and filesystem contract

- Crabshell is a kernel-mode serial shell with a separate parser crate; it is not a process or a security boundary.
- The RAM filesystem is volatile, bounded, and reset on reboot. It has no persistent block device, permissions, links, journaling, or general POSIX semantics.
- Preserve explicit path, capacity, and mutation errors. Do not add hidden truncation or destructive overwrite behavior.
- When adding a command, update parser syntax/tests, kernel execution/help, and `docs/architecture/crabshell.md`; update README examples if users will encounter it.

## Supported repository checks

Run commands from the repository root:

```sh
just fmt
just test
just check
just build
just image
just smoke
just verify
```

- `just fmt` checks workspace Rust formatting.
- `just test` runs host-side ACPI, paging, frame allocator, heap, IRQ/time/input/scheduler policy, VFS, and Crabshell parser tests.
- `just check` checks the freestanding `x86_64-unknown-none` target; it is not a final link.
- `just build` links the optimized kernel ELF.
- `just image` builds the hybrid ISO and may download the pinned Limine archive on first use.
- `just smoke` uses QEMU and checks that the shell prompt is reached.
- `just verify` combines formatting, host tests, target check, image creation, BIOS/OVMF boot, active-map, cooperative-thread, and UART/PS/2 input smokes.

Image and boot checks need Python 3, `xorriso`, QEMU, the Rust target, and network access for the initial pinned download. For changes to boot entry/requests, linker configuration, architecture code, frame allocation, paging, or heap code, the intended full validation is `just verify`. Report failed or unavailable commands exactly. Editor diagnostics are not a substitute for Cargo or QEMU evidence.

## Documentation to consult

- `docs/index.md` — project status and documentation map.
- `docs/roadmap/README.md` — milestone plan and exit criteria.
- `docs/architecture/overview.md` — architecture and layering.
- `docs/architecture/boot.md` — Limine handoff and boot snapshot.
- `docs/architecture/memory.md` — physical ranges, frame allocation, and paging direction.
- `docs/architecture/crabshell.md` — parser, shell commands, and RAM filesystem.
- `docs/architecture/drivers.md` — implemented drivers and limitations.
- `docs/security.md` — unsafe boundaries and security requirements.
- `docs/development/building.md` and `docs/development/testing.md` — build/test workflows and evidence policy.

# Claude Code instructions for Rustix

These are project-specific instructions for Claude Code and Claude-based agents working in this repository. `AGENTS.md` is the canonical shared engineering contract; read and follow it together with this file. If advice conflicts, preserve the stricter Rustix safety and validation rule, and do not infer that an unfinished subsystem is complete.

## What this repository is

Rustix is an experimental 64-bit Unix-like operating system with its own Rust kernel. The kernel is `no_std` and targets `x86_64-unknown-none`. Limine is only the external boot protocol/loader. Do not conflate the loader with Rustix or describe a host tool as the kernel.

The project is deliberately staged. Rustix currently boots to a kernel-mode Crabshell over COM1, with bounded IRQ input and a volatile RAM filesystem. A single-vCPU runtime supports cooperative waits/yields and timer preemption; this is not a userspace terminal, persistent filesystem, secure shell, or POSIX implementation. The `crabshell` workspace crate parses commands only; kernel I/O and filesystem operations remain in the kernel.

## Status must stay honest

Before planning a task, read `docs/roadmap/README.md` and the relevant architecture document. Milestones 0–3 have met their documented local exit criteria; the source includes:

- A Limine handoff and fixed-capacity owned boot snapshot with structural validation, CPUID/address-width reporting, and a classified memory map.
- A bounded physical-frame allocator, cloned active page-table hierarchy, kernel-image HHDM permission hardening, and a fixed BSS heap with bounded frame-backed growth.
- Bootstrap GDT/TSS/IDT and fatal exception stubs for vectors 0–31; double faults use an IST stack, and page faults report CR2/error bits.
- A validated single-vCPU xAPIC/I/O APIC path with masked-first IRQ routes, PIT ticks, EOI handling, and bounded UART/PS/2 IRQ input.
- A single-vCPU thread runtime with cooperative waits/yields and timer preemption, plus a separate allocation-free Crabshell parser and bounded volatile RAM filesystem.

Important limitations:

- Milestone 0–3 validation evidence is documented in `AGENTS.md` and `docs/roadmap/README.md`; it does not validate uncommitted changes in the current working tree.
- Structural boot checks cannot prove that a non-null Limine pointer is readable; the loader trust boundary remains.
- Scheduling is single-vCPU with cooperative waits/yields and timer preemption. There is no SMP, userspace, syscall ABI, persistent storage, user/kernel isolation, or general-purpose device model.
- Exceptions remain fatal-only. The shell and VFS run in ring 0 and are not isolated or secure.

Do not check off roadmap criteria merely because code or an interface exists. Only report builds, tests, and emulator checks that you actually ran and observed passing.

## Required workflow

1. Read `AGENTS.md`, the relevant `docs/architecture/*.md` document, and the actual implementation/call sites before changing code.
2. Identify the subsystem boundary and failure behavior. For hardware work, state assumptions about privilege level, selectors, page mappings, stack state, and IF/interrupt state before coding.
3. Make the smallest coherent vertical change. Prefer tested architecture-independent helpers in `src/lib.rs` modules over untestable freestanding-only logic when that preserves the design.
4. Add or update tests for normal, boundary, malformed, and exhaustion cases. Keep parser tests in `crates/crabshell`; do not make that crate depend on kernel facilities.
5. Update the relevant architecture, testing, security, and roadmap docs in the same change.
6. Run the narrow validation first, then the broader check appropriate to the touched paths.
7. In the final summary, distinguish implementation from verification and list any environmental blocker or remaining risk.

Do not commit, create branches, run broad formatting rewrites, or modify unrelated files unless explicitly requested.

## Rustix implementation rules

### `no_std` and fixed capacity

- Kernel code must remain freestanding and `no_std`; use `core`, not `std`.
- Avoid new Rust dependencies unless there is a concrete need and compatibility/security review.
- The global heap is bounded: a 256 KiB BSS arena plus up to 1 MiB of frame-backed growth. Allocation remains forbidden in IRQ/exception context; prefer fixed-capacity interfaces for core paths.
- Fixed-capacity tables must document capacity, exhaustion behavior, and whether an error leaves state unchanged.
- The kernel binary is not the host test target. Keep pure logic in the `rustix-kernel` library where practical.

### Boot, memory, and physical frames

- Limine writes response pointers before `_start`; response-bearing request records and their linker section must remain writable to the loader.
- Validate pointer nullness/alignment/counts and checked arithmetic, but preserve the documented trust boundary: Rustix cannot prove a loader pointer is mapped and readable.
- All physical ranges are half-open `[start, end)`. Use checked arithmetic and reject overlaps rather than silently normalizing malformed maps.
- Only `RegionKind::Usable` ranges feed the frame allocator. Reserved, ACPI, loader-reclaimable, framebuffer, bad, executable/module, and unknown ranges are never ordinary free frames.
- A frame handle represents a physical address; it is not a pointer. Do not dereference it, add the HHDM offset and assume success, or change CR3 until a reviewed mapping policy proves the access and ownership.
- The active root is an allocator-owned clone of Limine's reachable hierarchy. Any future replacement must preserve the executing kernel, boot stack, `BootInfo`, request/response objects, GDT/TSS/IDT data, exception stacks, and all mappings needed for continued execution.
- The current allocator is bounded and single-owner/single-core. It is not a page-table manager, heap, or concurrent allocator.

### x86_64 and exceptions

- Keep privileged instructions, port I/O, assembly, and raw pointer operations in narrow architecture modules with nearby safety comments.
- Exception handling remains fatal-only. The validated single-vCPU APIC path enables only configured, registered routes after IRQ dispatch and EOI setup. Timer preemption saves/restores x87/SSE state with FXSAVE/FXRSTOR; AVX/XSAVE remains disabled.
- Do not broaden IRQ use, add exception recovery, or add SMP without an explicit design, ownership/locking rules, fault injection, and emulator validation.
- When editing `src/arch/x86_64/interrupts.rs`, review normalized CPU-error-code stack layout, register-save ordering, stack alignment before calling Rust, the double-fault IST, descriptor selectors, and fatal behavior. Assembly diagnostics are not a substitute for assembling/linking the target.
- `CPUID` support bits do not prove a feature is enabled in control registers or active page tables. Label reports as supported/capable unless activation is verified.

### Crabshell and VFS

- The parser crate may contain syntax/model types, but no terminal, VFS, kernel, or hardware I/O.
- Kernel command execution belongs in `src/shell.rs`; the fixed-capacity VFS contract belongs in `src/vfs.rs`.
- RAM filesystem contents disappear on reset. Preserve explicit errors, root protection, directory rules, path limits, node limits, and file-size limits.
- When adding/changing a command, update parser behavior/tests, shell execution/help, `docs/architecture/crabshell.md`, and user-facing examples as appropriate.

## Supported validation

Run these from the repository root using `just`:

```sh
just fmt
just test
just check
just build
just image
just smoke
just verify
```

`just test` runs host tests for ACPI parsing, paging and mapping policy, frame allocation, heap, IRQ/time/input/scheduler policy, VFS, and Crabshell parsing. `just check` type-checks `x86_64-unknown-none`; `just build` links the release ELF. `just verify` covers formatting, host tests, target check, pinned Limine image creation, BIOS/OVMF boot, active-map, cooperative-thread, and UART/PS/2 input QEMU smokes. Image/boot steps need Python 3, `xorriso`, QEMU, OVMF, the target, and network access for the first pinned download.

Changes to boot requests/entry, `linker.ld`, `src/arch/x86_64/`, memory allocation, paging, or heap code should receive `just verify` when the environment permits. If it does not, report the exact command failure and leave the corresponding roadmap criterion unchecked.

Editor diagnostics are useful but are not proof that Rust compiled, assembly assembled, the target linked, the image booted, or the hardware path works. Never say “tests pass” when they were not run.

## Relevant documentation

- `docs/index.md` — documentation entry point and current status.
- `docs/roadmap/README.md` — sequencing and milestone exit criteria.
- `docs/architecture/overview.md` — architecture and subsystem layering.
- `docs/architecture/boot.md` — Limine request/response contract and trust boundary.
- `docs/architecture/memory.md` — ranges, frame allocator, inherited mappings, and future paging.
- `docs/architecture/crabshell.md` — parser, commands, and RAM filesystem contract.
- `docs/architecture/drivers.md` — driver status and scope.
- `docs/security.md` — unsafe boundaries and security requirements.
- `docs/development/building.md`, `docs/development/testing.md` — commands and evidence expectations.

```
//! Interrupt-safe spin locks for shared kernel state.
//!
//! Lock acquisition saves and disables local maskable interrupts before
//! spinning. Dropping the guard releases the lock before restoring the caller's
//! previous interrupt state, so nested critical sections do not enable IRQs
//! early. This provides local IRQ reentrancy protection and atomic exclusion;
//! it does not by itself make scheduler or device state safe for SMP.

use core::cell::UnsafeCell;
use core::hint::spin_loop;
use core::marker::PhantomData;
use core::ops::{Deref, DerefMut};
use core::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};

/// A spin lock that masks local interrupts for the full guard lifetime.
pub struct IrqSpinLock<T> {
    locked: AtomicBool,
    value: UnsafeCell<T>,
}

// SAFETY: Access to `value` is exclusive while the atomic lock is held. The
// protected value must be transferable between CPUs, as required by spin locks.
unsafe impl<T: Send> Sync for IrqSpinLock<T> {}

impl<T> IrqSpinLock<T> {
    pub const fn new(value: T) -> Self {
        Self {
            locked: AtomicBool::new(false),
            value: UnsafeCell::new(value),
        }
    }

    /// Acquire the lock with local maskable interrupts disabled.
    pub fn lock(&self) -> IrqSpinLockGuard<'_, T> {
        let interrupt_flags = save_and_disable_interrupts();
        while self
            .locked
            .compare_exchange_weak(false, true, Ordering::Acquire, Ordering::Relaxed)
            .is_err()
        {
            spin_loop();
        }
        IrqSpinLockGuard {
            lock: self,
            interrupt_flags,
            _not_send: PhantomData,
        }
    }
}

/// Exclusive access to the value protected by an [`IrqSpinLock`].
pub struct IrqSpinLockGuard<'a, T> {
    lock: &'a IrqSpinLock<T>,
    interrupt_flags: u64,
    _not_send: PhantomData<*mut ()>,
}

impl<T> Deref for IrqSpinLockGuard<'_, T> {
    type Target = T;

    fn deref(&self) -> &Self::Target {
        // SAFETY: The guard holds the lock for its full lifetime.
        unsafe { &*self.lock.value.get() }
    }
}

impl<T> DerefMut for IrqSpinLockGuard<'_, T> {
    fn deref_mut(&mut self) -> &mut Self::Target {
        // SAFETY: The guard holds the lock for its full lifetime and cannot be
        // sent to another CPU.
        unsafe { &mut *self.lock.value.get() }
    }
}

impl<T> Drop for IrqSpinLockGuard<'_, T> {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        self.lock.locked.store(false, Ordering::Release);
        restore_interrupts(self.interrupt_flags);
    }
}

#[cfg(all(target_arch = "x86_64", target_os = "none"))]
fn save_and_disable_interrupts() -> u64 {
    let flags: u64;
    // SAFETY: Kernel callers execute at CPL 0; the stack operation is balanced.
    // The asm's memory effects also keep protected accesses inside the guard.
    unsafe { core::arch::asm!("pushfq", "pop {}", "cli", out(reg) flags) };
    flags
}

#[cfg(not(all(target_arch = "x86_64", target_os = "none")))]
fn save_and_disable_interrupts() -> u64 {
    // Host tests exercise lock exclusion; privileged IF manipulation is only
    // available in the freestanding x86_64 kernel.
    0
}

#[cfg(all(target_arch = "x86_64", target_os = "none"))]
fn restore_interrupts(flags: u64) {
    if flags & (1 << 9) != 0 {
        // SAFETY: The guard released its lock before restoring the prior IF state.
        unsafe { core::arch::asm!("sti") };
    }
}

#[cfg(not(all(target_arch = "x86_64", target_os = "none")))]
fn restore_interrupts(_flags: u64) {}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::IrqSpinLock;
    use core::assert_eq;

    #[test]
    fn guard_provides_exclusive_mutable_access_and_releases_lock() {
        let lock = IrqSpinLock::new(1usize);
        {
            let mut value = lock.lock();
            *value += 2;
            assert_eq!(*value, 3);
        }
        assert_eq!(*lock.lock(), 3);
    }

    #[test]
    fn nested_guards_preserve_lock_contents() {
        let outer = IrqSpinLock::new(4usize);
        let inner = IrqSpinLock::new(7usize);
        let mut outer_guard = outer.lock();
        let mut inner_guard = inner.lock();
        *outer_guard += *inner_guard;
        *inner_guard += 1;
        assert_eq!(*outer_guard, 11);
        assert_eq!(*inner_guard, 8);
    }
}

```
Rustix now boots into **Crabshell**, a small kernel-mode shell on the COM1 serial terminal. It includes basic navigation and file commands backed by a fixed-capacity RAM filesystem. The filesystem is volatile and reset at every boot; this is an early kernel shell, not a userspace process or POSIX shell. The command parser lives in a separate, allocation-free `crabshell` crate so a future GUI terminal can reuse it. Single-vCPU cooperative scheduling and bounded UART/PS/2 IRQ input are present; timer preemption, process isolation, persistent storage, a syscall ABI, networking, and userspace remain future work. See [`docs/roadmap/README.md`](docs/roadmap/README.md) for the staged plan.

    17	pub struct ByteRing<const CAPACITY: usize> {
    18	    bytes: [AtomicU8; CAPACITY],
    19	    head: AtomicUsize,
    20	    tail: AtomicUsize,
    21	    // Physical slot positions wrap at CAPACITY, independently of counter wrap.
    22	    head_index: AtomicUsize,
    23	    tail_index: AtomicUsize,

    25	}
